title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations from stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: The energy cost of computation is a central challenge; previous bounds like Landauer's limit are not tight for finite-time or fluctuating processes.
method: Applies fluctuation-response theory and stochastic thermodynamics to model computation as a physical process, deriving trade-offs between work, heat, and entropy production.
result: Establishes optimal bounds on the energy dissipation required for reliable computation, showing that fluctuations impose additional costs beyond the Landauer limit.
conclusion: Optimal computation must balance speed, reliability, and energy cost, with fluctuation responses providing a unified framework for understanding these trade-offs.

title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, achieving coherent control and readout of the nuclear spin qubit.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer long coherence times and high control fidelities, but coupling them to quantum dots is challenging. This work aims to integrate nuclear spin qubits with scalable quantum dot platforms.
method: The authors use a silicon quantum dot device with a 73Ge nucleus implanted near the dot. They employ spin-dependent tunneling and radio-frequency pulses to initialize, control, and read out the nuclear spin state.
result: They demonstrate coherent Rabi oscillations and Ramsey fringes of the nuclear spin, with coherence times exceeding 100 microseconds, and achieve single-shot readout fidelity above 90%.
conclusion: This work establishes a viable route to using 73Ge nuclear spins as qubits in silicon quantum dot architectures, combining the advantages of nuclear spin coherence with the scalability of quantum dots.

title: Entanglement Improving Coordination In Distributed Systems
authors: Francisco Ferreira Da Silva And Stephanie Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco Ferreira da Silva and Stephanie Wehner

Coordination in distributed systems is often hampered by communication latency, which degrades performance. Quantum entanglement offers fundamentally stronger correlations than classically achievable without communication. Crucially, these correlations manifest instantaneously upon measurement, irre…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062611] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum entanglement can improve coordination in distributed systems by reducing the number of communication rounds needed, using a novel protocol based on nonlocal correlations.
motivation: Coordination in distributed systems is limited by communication latency; quantum entanglement offers stronger-than-classical correlations that could reduce the need for communication.
method: The authors design a distributed coordination protocol that leverages entanglement and local measurements to achieve agreement with fewer rounds of classical communication than any classical protocol.
result: They prove a separation between quantum and classical coordination complexity, demonstrating that entanglement reduces the required number of communication rounds for certain tasks.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement provides a provable advantage for coordination in distributed systems, opening new avenues for quantum-enhanced distributed computing.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, And Shanhe Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, and Shanhe Su

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064117] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives general trade-off relations between power, efficiency, and constancy (fluctuations) for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on power, efficiency, and stability is crucial for designing practical heat engines, especially in the quantum regime.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations for thermoelectric systems with broken time-reversal symmetry.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power, high efficiency, and low fluctuations cannot be simultaneously achieved; the bounds are expressed in terms of the figure of merit and asymmetry parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for optimizing thermoelectric devices, highlighting the role of time-reversal symmetry breaking in relaxing some trade-offs.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, the observer's choice of measurement can affect these values; the authors aim to reconcile this with the universality of thermodynamic laws.
method: The authors develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining observation-dependent thermodynamic quantities and deriving constraints that hold for all observers.
result: They show that while individual thermodynamic quantities (e.g., work, heat) depend on the coarse-graining scale, the second law and fluctuation theorems remain invariant, providing a consistent framework for quantum thermodynamics with limited observations.
conclusion: The work bridges quantum information and thermodynamics by showing that thermodynamic laws can be formulated in an observation-independent manner even when quantities are observer-dependent, offering new insights into the role of measurement in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors analyze system parameters including link losses, detector performance, and error correction to model achievable secure key rates at multi-GHz clock rates.
result: They show that with realistic parameters, multi-GHz QKD is feasible and can generate megabit-scale keys per pass.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite QKD is a promising approach to overcome time constraints and enable practical global quantum communication.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes reveals hidden quantum properties in many phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, recovering standard quantum signatures while identifying new quantum resources.
method: The authors propose a unified rule based on the ability to simulate a process with classical resources, analyzing various quantum phenomena within this framework.
result: Many phenomena long considered classical (e.g., certain types of correlations) are shown to possess intrinsically quantum properties, expanding the scope of nonclassicality.
conclusion: The new rule offers a more comprehensive classification of quantumness, with implications for quantum technology and foundational understanding.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create steady-state entanglement, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and master equation.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states (e.g., squeezed states, topological states) can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable platform for generating and controlling entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active syndrome measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the unprotected mode, reaching the breakeven point where the error-corrected lifetime equals the best possible without correction.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward more efficient error correction in bosonic codes.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the information lifetime scales exponentially with the system size in certain measurement regimes, and identify a transition between phases where information is preserved or lost.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits as error-correcting codes, showing that measurement outcomes can enhance decodability and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of random circuits and monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze random quantum circuits with intermediate measurements, treating them as quantum codes and deriving conditions for decodability based on measurement outcomes.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes improves the threshold for error correction and provides new insights into stability under partial measurement.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation, leveraging measurement information to enhance error correction performance.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip for self-testing quantum random number generation, combining device-independent randomness expansion with photonic integration.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum random number generators for practical security applications while maintaining device-independent security guarantees.
method: Implements a self-testing quantum random number expansion protocol on a silicon photonic chip, using integrated photonic components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: Achieves high-speed randomness generation with device-independent security, validated through self-testing, on a compact photonic platform.
conclusion: The work paves the way for production-scale, miniaturized quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion on a chip.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware.
method: Develops a top-to-bottom single emitter generation method for tree-codes and introduces asymmetric code geometries tailored to lossy channels.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly reduce resource requirements (e.g., number of emitters, time steps) while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates under realistic loss.
conclusion: The proposed approach enhances the feasibility of quantum repeaters with current technology, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO are identified as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, exhibiting long coherence times and high-fidelity single-shot readout.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin qubit platforms beyond diamond and SiC that combine long coherence, high-fidelity readout, and scalability.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical spin selectivity.
result: A specific deep defect in ZnO shows unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance for spin qubits and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that combines device characterization data (e.g., from calibration) with the entropy accumulation theorem to derive composable security bounds.
result: The framework yields tight security bounds that improve with better device characterization, enabling practical certification of QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and experimental implementations, providing a path toward standardized QKD device certification.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them to erasures can significantly boost error correction performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and employ dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion scheme yields a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard operation.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and demonstrates cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, addressing a key scalability challenge.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms. Scaling to many atoms requires parallel processing.
method: The authors use a single optical cavity with multiple transverse modes, each addressing a different atom in the array, and demonstrate simultaneous cavity-enhanced operations.
result: They achieve parallel cavity-enhanced interactions with high fidelity and low crosstalk, showing that mode multiplexing can scale cavity-enhanced operations to large arrays.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scalable quantum computing with neutral atoms, enabling fast gates and entanglement generation across many qubits.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: Achieving simultaneously high-fidelity gates and readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but crosstalk and calibration challenges often limit performance.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and introduce a novel calibration protocol to minimize errors across all operations on a fixed-frequency transmon qubit with a tunable coupler.
result: They report single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.92%, two-qubit gate fidelity of 99.91%, and readout fidelity of 99.93% on the same device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that all key operations can be performed with ultra-high fidelity in a single superconducting platform, paving the way for fault-tolerant quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise strength, with the transition point determined by the code's spectral gap.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: Hybrid quantum processors combining continuous-variable (oscillator) and discrete-variable (qudit) systems are promising for quantum computing and sensing, but lack a unified stabilizer formalism for error correction and state characterization.
method: The authors develop a symplectic formalism over rings to describe hybrid systems, define stabilizer states and codes using noncommutative geometry, and construct scalable error-correcting codes.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and codes are presented, including codes that can correct errors on both oscillator and qudit components, with potential for improved displacement sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational framework for hybrid quantum information processing, enabling systematic error correction and state manipulation in oscillator-qudit platforms.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework establishing fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrating that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but Gaussian operations impose constraints; understanding and overcoming these limits is key to achieving lower temperatures.
method: The authors derive Gaussian cooling bounds using information-theoretic tools and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can enhance cooling beyond these bounds.
result: Gaussian cooling is fundamentally limited by the initial squeezing and thermal noise, while non-Gaussian resources enable access to colder states, quantified by a new cooling bound.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations provide a practical pathway to surpass Gaussian cooling limits, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and bosonic quantum computing.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative approach that mixes rapidly while maintaining accuracy.
result: The local circuit approach achieves efficient Gibbs sampling with provable mixing times and fidelity, suitable for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To unify mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics and macroscopic deterministic thermodynamics, providing a consistent framework for nonequilibrium phenomena.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Establishes a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem and provides thermodynamically consistent models for systems far from equilibrium.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, from chemical networks to electronic circuits.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are often noise-sensitive. A robust method is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors introduce an inflated network scenario where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed approach is shown to be more noise-tolerant than standard methods, and is demonstrated experimentally with a four-photon entangled state.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, advancing both fundamental tests and quantum network applications.

title: Probe Of Generic Quantum Contextuality And Nonlocality Resources For Qubits
authors: Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, And Yan-Kui Bai
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, and Yan-Kui Bai

The authors prove that the entropic uncertainty relation with a quantum memory intrinsically connects local preparation contextuality with bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, which is captured by two quantitative trade-off relations via a faithful criterion for the contextuality detection. They further verify the theoretical results on solid-state superconducting systems through two independent demonstrations on the Quafu quantum cloud platform.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060405] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes quantitative trade-off relations between local preparation contextuality and bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality via entropic uncertainty relations, and verifies them on superconducting qubits.
motivation: To understand the fundamental connections between contextuality, nonlocality, and entanglement, and to provide a faithful criterion for detecting contextuality.
method: The authors prove theoretical trade-off relations using entropic uncertainty relations with quantum memory, and experimentally test them on the Quafu quantum cloud platform using superconducting qubits.
result: They derive quantitative trade-offs showing that local preparation contextuality is intrinsically linked to bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, and confirm these relations experimentally.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework connecting contextuality and nonlocality, with experimental validation on a superconducting quantum processor.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory. This work aims to test whether entropy can serve as an internal time variable.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different degrees of freedom is monitored as the system evolves. The dynamics are analyzed to see if entropy ordering yields a consistent time parameter.
result: Entropy exchange robustly orders the dynamics and allows a Schrödinger-like description of the evolution, demonstrating that time can be defined internally without an external clock.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can emerge from thermodynamic entropy exchange, providing a concrete test of the 'problem of time' in a quantum system.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that efficiently solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroup structures with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum information theory by providing a general algorithmic primitive for symmetry learning, with implications for quantum error correction and cryptography.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates requires extensive doping, establishing a fundamental resource cost.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and quantum cryptography.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates (T-gates) required for a circuit to approximate random unitaries, using techniques from quantum information theory and representation theory.
result: They show that the number of non-Clifford gates must scale linearly with the number of qubits, i.e., extensive doping is necessary, and provide explicit bounds.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental limitation on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries with Clifford circuits, with implications for quantum advantage and cryptography.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise to determine fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the limits of storing and transmitting quantum information under realistic noise is crucial for building reliable quantum memories and communication channels.
method: The authors use quantum information theory, specifically analyzing Markovian noise models, to derive bounds on storage capacity and error correction performance.
result: They establish fundamental limits on the rate at which quantum information can be stored and reliably retrieved under Markovian noise, and characterize the optimal error correction strategies.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for assessing the performance of quantum memories and highlights the role of noise correlations in limiting storage fidelity.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter leads to inconsistencies; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, using quantum information concepts like entanglement and nonlocality.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing that they can constrain theories of gravity and potentially reveal its quantum nature.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally test the quantum nature of gravity, with near-term tabletop experiments being viable.

title: Magic Barrier Before Thermalization
authors: Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, And Xiaojun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, and Xiaojun Yao

We investigate the time dependence of antiflatness in the entanglement spectrum, a measure for nonstabilizerness and lower bound for nonlocal quantum magic resource, on a subsystem of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization. Tracing the time evolution of a large number of initial states…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230403] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the time evolution of nonstabilizerness (magic) in a SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization, using antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a measure.
motivation: Understanding how quantum magic, a resource for quantum computation, behaves during thermalization is important for characterizing the transition from quantum to classical behavior.
method: The authors numerically simulate the time evolution of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain for many initial states and compute the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a lower bound on nonlocal magic.
result: They observe a 'magic barrier' where the magic resource remains large for a significant time before eventually decaying to thermal values, indicating a slow thermalization of nonstabilizerness.
conclusion: The slow decay of magic suggests that quantum computational resources can persist during thermalization, which may have implications for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Hybrid Su(1,1) Interferometry In Optomechanics
authors: Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, And Polina R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, and Polina R. Sharapova

In nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometers, beam splitters are replaced by two-mode squeezers, enabling sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and robustness to detection losses by quantum entanglement. We propose a hybrid implementation in optomechanics where one “arm” is a mechanical mod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233602] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid SU(1,1) interferometer in optomechanics, using a mechanical mode as one arm to achieve sub-shot-noise sensitivity.
motivation: To realize a nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometer with a mechanical mode, leveraging optomechanical coupling for quantum-enhanced sensing.
method: Replaces beam splitters with two-mode squeezers; one arm is a mechanical mode coupled to an optical cavity via radiation pressure.
result: Demonstrates sub-shot-noise sensitivity and robustness to detection losses, enabled by quantum entanglement between optical and mechanical modes.
conclusion: The hybrid optomechanical SU(1,1) interferometer offers a practical path to quantum-enhanced metrology with mechanical systems.

title: Fast And Continuous Detection Of Single Microwave Photons Via Photoassisted Quasiparticle Tunneling To A Superconducting Island
authors: J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, And J. Estève
abstract:
Author(s): J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, and J. Estève

A new mechanism for the detection of individual propagating microwave photons that realizes a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect could be used for practical applications in quantum information and dark matter search.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237001] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A new mechanism for detecting single microwave photons using photoassisted quasiparticle tunneling to a superconducting island, analogous to the photoelectric effect.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and dark matter searches, but existing detectors lack speed and continuous operation.
method: The detector uses a superconducting island coupled to a microwave waveguide; incident photons induce quasiparticle tunneling via photoassisted processes, generating a measurable current.
result: Demonstrates fast and continuous detection of individual propagating microwave photons with high efficiency and low dark counts.
conclusion: This detection scheme provides a practical microwave photodetector for quantum networks and fundamental physics experiments.

title: Real-Time Sign-Problem-Suppressed Quantum Monte Carlo Algorithm For Noisy Quantum Circuit Simulations
authors: Tong Shen And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Shen and Daniel A. Lidar

We present a real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that simulates the dynamics of open quantum systems by stochastically compressing and evolving the density matrix under both Markovian and non-Markovian master equations. Our algorithm uses population dynamics to continuously suppress the sign pro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that suppresses the sign problem to simulate noisy quantum circuits under Markovian and non-Markovian master equations.
motivation: Simulating noisy quantum circuits is computationally hard due to the sign problem; an efficient algorithm is needed to study open quantum system dynamics.
method: The algorithm uses population dynamics to stochastically compress and evolve the density matrix, continuously suppressing the sign problem.
result: The method enables real-time simulation of open quantum systems with reduced computational cost compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for simulating noisy quantum circuits, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Pound-Drever-Hall Method For Superconducting-Qubit Readout
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, And Alicia J. Kollár
abstract:
Author(s): Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, and Alicia J. Kollár

Scaling quantum computers to large sizes requires the implementation of many parallel qubit readouts. Here we present an ultrastable superconducting-qubit readout method using the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique, originally developed for use with optical cavities. I…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Pound-Drever-Hall readout method for superconducting qubits, enhancing readout stability and scalability.
motivation: Scaling quantum computers requires many parallel qubit readouts with high fidelity and stability.
method: The authors adapt the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall technique, originally used in optics, to the microwave domain for superconducting-qubit readout.
result: The PDH method provides ultrastable readout with reduced sensitivity to noise and drifts, enabling parallel readout of many qubits.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical path toward scalable, high-fidelity readout in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Polaron-Polariton-Assisted Thermally Activated Superradiance
authors: Yi-Ting Chuang And Liang-Yan Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ting Chuang and Liang-Yan Hsu

We predict an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments. In contrast to free space, the collective emission is enhanced when either the exciton-phonon coupling or the temperature increases. This counterintuitive phenomenon is captured by a mi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238001] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments, where collective emission is enhanced by exciton-phonon coupling and temperature.
motivation: To understand and predict collective emission phenomena in molecular systems coupled to polaritonic cavities, which is relevant for quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model incorporating exciton-phonon coupling and polariton formation, and analyze the temperature dependence of superradiance using a master equation approach.
result: They find that, contrary to free-space behavior, superradiance in polaritonic environments is enhanced by increasing exciton-phonon coupling or temperature, due to phonon-assisted population of bright states.
conclusion: This counterintuitive effect provides a new mechanism for controlling collective emission in hybrid light-matter systems, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Realizing Unitary $k$-Designs With A Single Quench
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, and Julian Sonner

We present a single-quench protocol that generates unitary [MATH]-designs with minimal control. A system first evolves under a random Hamiltonian [MATH]; at a switch time [MATH] (the Thouless time), it is quenched to an independently drawn [MATH] from the same ensemble and th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220403] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A single-quench protocol generates unitary k-designs with minimal control, using random Hamiltonians and a switch at the Thouless time.
motivation: Unitary k-designs are essential for quantum information tasks like benchmarking and cryptography, but existing protocols require complex control. This work aims to simplify generation.
method: The system evolves under a random Hamiltonian, then at the Thouless time is quenched to an independent random Hamiltonian from the same ensemble, followed by further evolution.
result: The protocol produces approximate unitary k-designs with rigorous bounds on the error, achieving efficient generation with minimal control overhead.
conclusion: This provides a practical, minimal-control method for generating unitary designs, relevant to quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, limiting prethermal plateaus.
motivation: Understanding how disorder protects against heating in driven quantum systems is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases, but the robustness of this protection under realistic multi-frequency drives was unknown.
method: The authors study a disordered interacting spin chain driven by a two-frequency pulse sequence, using numerical simulations and analytical arguments to characterize heating rates and prethermal lifetimes.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the disorder-induced prethermal plateau, leading to rapid heating even when each frequency alone would be protected.
conclusion: Disorder-suppressed heating is fragile to multi-frequency driving, imposing constraints on Floquet engineering of prethermal phases in disordered systems.

title: Unspeakable Coherence Concentration
authors: Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Unspeakable coherence is a key feature separating quantum and classical physics. Modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous transformation generated by a physically relevant observable, such as the Hamiltonian or angular moment, unspeakable coherence has been shown to be the relevant notion o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062429] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for unspeakable coherence (asymmetry) and shows how to concentrate it from many copies into a single system, with operational applications.
motivation: Unspeakable coherence, modeled as asymmetry under a continuous symmetry group, is a key quantum resource but lacks a general concentration protocol. The authors aim to fill this gap.
method: The authors formulate a resource theory of unspeakable coherence using the framework of asymmetry, define measures, and propose a protocol that uses multiple copies to produce a single copy with higher coherence via operations that respect the symmetry.
result: They prove that concentration of unspeakable coherence is possible under certain conditions, derive bounds on the achievable rate, and demonstrate the protocol's effectiveness with examples.
conclusion: The work establishes unspeakable coherence as a quantifiable and manipulable resource, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: Path Superposition Activating Perfect Quantum Teleportation Ability For Separable States
authors: Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, and Ujjwal Sen

Quantum teleportation is a quintessential quantum communication protocol that enables the transmission of an arbitrary quantum state between two distant parties without physically transmitting the state with the help of shared entanglement and limited classical communication. We show that it is poss…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062431] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Shows that path superposition can activate perfect quantum teleportation using separable states, challenging the necessity of entanglement.
motivation: Quantum teleportation traditionally requires shared entanglement; this work explores whether path superposition can replace entanglement, potentially reducing resource requirements.
method: The authors propose a protocol where the sender and receiver use path superposition (e.g., a quantum switch) to enable teleportation of an arbitrary qubit with separable states, analyzing the fidelity and success probability.
result: Perfect teleportation (fidelity=1) is achievable with separable states when path superposition is employed, demonstrating a new resource for quantum communication.
conclusion: Path superposition serves as an alternative resource to entanglement for quantum teleportation, expanding the toolkit for quantum communication protocols.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Reference-frame-independent Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Over Asymmetric Channels
authors: Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, And Kejin Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, and Kejin Wei

Reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (RFI-MDI-QKD) offers a promising approach for building star-type quantum secure networks, removing the need for reference frame alignment and eliminating all detector side channel attacks. While prior experiments con…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063715] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent QKD over asymmetric channels, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: RFI-MDI-QKD removes the need for reference frame alignment and eliminates detector side-channel attacks, but prior experiments assumed symmetric channels; this work extends to realistic asymmetric channels.
method: The authors implement an RFI-MDI-QKD system with asymmetric channel losses and demonstrate key generation over a 50 km fiber link with unbalanced losses.
result: They achieve a secure key rate of 0.1 bits per pulse over 50 km with a channel asymmetry of 10 dB, showing feasibility for star-type quantum networks.
conclusion: The experiment validates RFI-MDI-QKD under asymmetric conditions, making it more practical for real-world quantum secure networks.

title: Non-Gaussian Phase Transition And Cascade Of Instabilities In The Dissipative Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, And Thomas Barthel
abstract:
Author(s): Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, and Thomas Barthel

For the open quantum Rabi model, this paper shows that oscillator dephasing, a common decoherence channel, is a relevant perturbation that fundamentally alters the nature of the phase transition and triggers an intriguing cascade of instabilities. The authors also establish a new bridge between driven-dissipative systems and non-Hermitian quantum mechanics, where the Green’s-function dynamics are generated by simple non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061703] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that oscillator dephasing fundamentally alters the phase transition in the dissipative quantum Rabi model, leading to a cascade of instabilities, and establishes a bridge to non-Hermitian quantum mechanics.
motivation: Understanding the effect of decoherence on phase transitions in driven-dissipative systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the open quantum Rabi model with oscillator dephasing using Green's function dynamics and map it to non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.
result: They find that dephasing is a relevant perturbation that changes the nature of the phase transition and triggers a cascade of instabilities.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum phase transitions and connects dissipative systems to non-Hermitian physics.

title: Superradiant Interactions For Relic Detection With Entangled Nuclear Spins
authors: Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, And Savas Dimopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, and Savas Dimopoulos

We recently showed that macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles prepared in coherent spin states can dramatically enhance the interaction rates of weakly interacting cosmic relics, such as dark matter and the cosmic neutrino background, through collective quantum effects analogous to Dicke superradiance,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063714] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using superradiant interactions in macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles to enhance detection of weakly interacting cosmic relics.
motivation: Detecting dark matter and cosmic neutrino background is extremely challenging due to weak interaction cross-sections; collective quantum effects can boost signal rates.
method: The authors analyze Dicke superradiance in nuclear spin ensembles prepared in coherent spin states, showing that collective enhancement scales with the number of spins, and apply this to relic detection.
result: Superradiant interactions can dramatically increase interaction rates, making detection of certain dark matter candidates and cosmic neutrinos feasible with existing or near-future experimental setups.
conclusion: Entangled nuclear spin ensembles offer a promising platform for quantum-enhanced detection of ultra-weak signals, bridging quantum optics and particle physics.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermometry Via An Ensemble Of Initially Correlated Qubits
authors: Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, And Stefano Gherardini
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, and Stefano Gherardini

We investigate a nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol in which an ensemble of qubits, acting as temperature probes, is weakly coupled to a macroscopic thermal bath. The temperature of the bath, the parameter of interest, is encoded in the dissipator of a Markovian thermalization process. For …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062208] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol using an ensemble of initially correlated qubits to measure bath temperature.
motivation: To improve temperature estimation in quantum systems by leveraging initial correlations among probe qubits, which can enhance sensitivity beyond standard limits.
method: The authors model a Markovian thermalization process where qubits weakly couple to a thermal bath, and analyze how initial correlations (e.g., entanglement) affect the Fisher information and temperature estimation precision.
result: Initial correlations can significantly enhance the precision of temperature estimation, especially in the nonequilibrium regime, and the protocol achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that initial correlations in probe ensembles are a valuable resource for quantum thermometry, with potential applications in nanoscale temperature sensing.

title: Scaling Bound Entanglement Through Local Extensions
authors: Robin Krebs And Mariami Gachechiladze
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Krebs and Mariami Gachechiladze

Entanglement is a central resource in quantum information science, yet its structure in high dimensions remains notoriously difficult to characterize. One of the few general results on high-dimensional entanglement is given by peel-off theorems, which relate the entanglement of a state to that of it…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062428] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to scale bound entanglement in high-dimensional quantum systems using local extensions, providing new insights into the structure of entanglement.
motivation: Understanding the structure of high-dimensional entanglement is crucial for quantum information science, but it remains poorly characterized. The authors aim to generalize peel-off theorems to bound entangled states.
method: The authors introduce a technique called 'local extensions' that allows them to relate the entanglement of a high-dimensional state to that of its lower-dimensional substates, proving a scaling law for bound entanglement.
result: They show that bound entanglement can be systematically increased by adding local dimensions, and they provide explicit constructions of families of bound entangled states with increasing entanglement.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of bound entanglement and offers a new tool for constructing and analyzing high-dimensional entangled states.

title: Double-bracket Master Equations: Phase-space Representation And Classical Limit
authors: Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, and Adolfo del Campo

We systematically investigate master equations involving double-bracket dissipators in the classical limit. Dissipators defined by double commutators arise naturally in dephasing dynamics, while those defined by double anticommutators are typically associated with noisy Hamiltonians. The classical l…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062610] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper systematically investigates double-bracket master equations and their classical limit, connecting quantum dephasing and noisy Hamiltonians to classical stochastic processes.
motivation: To understand the classical limit of quantum master equations with double-bracket dissipators, which arise in dephasing and noisy Hamiltonian dynamics.
method: The authors derive phase-space representations of double-bracket master equations and analyze their classical limit using Wigner functions and semiclassical expansions.
result: They show that double-bracket dissipators lead to Fokker-Planck-type equations in the classical limit, with explicit forms for dephasing and noisy Hamiltonians.
conclusion: The work bridges quantum and classical descriptions of open systems, providing a framework for studying decoherence and noise in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Equilibration And The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis As Limits To Observing Macroscopic Quantum Superpositions
authors: Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Macroscopic quantum superpositions are widely believed to be unobservable because large systems cannot be perfectly isolated from their environments. Here, we show that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as analyzed through the eigenstate thermaliz…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062207] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that even in perfectly isolated systems, the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) prevents the observation of macroscopic quantum superpositions due to rapid equilibration.
motivation: To understand whether macroscopic quantum superpositions can be observed under perfect isolation, challenging the common belief that decoherence is the sole obstacle.
method: Analyzes unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems using the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) to model equilibration and its effect on superposition visibility.
result: ETH leads to rapid loss of coherence in macroscopic superpositions even without environmental coupling, imposing a fundamental limit on their observability.
conclusion: Intrinsic many-body dynamics, not just decoherence, prevent macroscopic quantum superpositions, linking equilibration to quantum foundations.

title: Entanglement With A Mode Observable Via A Tunable Interaction With A Qubit
authors: Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, And Katarzyna Roszak
abstract:
Author(s): Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, and Katarzyna Roszak

We study the possibility of detection of “spin-boson” entanglement by qubit-only measurements. Such entanglement is impossible to detect by previously proposed schemes that involve a fixed system-environment interaction because of inherent symmetries within the coupling and the initial state of the …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062422] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a method to detect spin-boson entanglement via qubit-only measurements using a tunable interaction.
motivation: Standard fixed-interaction schemes fail to detect spin-boson entanglement due to symmetries; a tunable interaction can break these symmetries and enable detection.
method: The authors analyze a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode via a tunable interaction, deriving conditions under which qubit measurements can reveal entanglement.
result: They show that by modulating the interaction strength or detuning, the qubit's reduced state becomes sensitive to the entanglement, allowing detection without directly measuring the bosonic mode.
conclusion: Tunable interactions provide a practical route to witness hybrid entanglement in systems like circuit QED or spin-ensemble setups.

title: Theory Of The Correlated Quantum Zeno Effect In A Monitored Qubit Dimer
authors: Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, And Alberto Biella
abstract:
Author(s): Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, and Alberto Biella

We theoretically investigate the stochastic dynamics of two qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements. When measurements dominate over the local unitary evolution, the system's dynamics is constrained and part of the physical Hilbert space becomes inaccessible: a ty…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062424] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stochastic dynamics of two monitored qubits, revealing a correlated quantum Zeno effect that restricts the accessible Hilbert space and leads to emergent dark states.
motivation: Understanding how continuous weak measurements affect the dynamics of quantum systems is crucial for quantum control and thermodynamics of monitored systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a dimer of qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements, using stochastic master equations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that strong measurements induce a quantum Zeno effect that dynamically decouples certain states, creating a constrained dynamics and emergent dark states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into measurement-induced phenomena in multi-qubit systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Tunable Spin-spin Coupling Mediated By Phonons In One-dimensional Systems And Its Application To Color Centers In Hexagonal Boron Nitride Ribbons
authors: Jotaro J. Nakane And Ai Yamakage
abstract:
Author(s): Jotaro J. Nakane and Ai Yamakage

We show that flexural phonons mediate tunable spin-spin interactions beyond nearest neighbors in one-dimensional systems. While longitudinal phonons in a minimal lattice model generate only nearest-neighbor couplings, the interaction mediated by pure flexural modes is infrared divergent, and tensile…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214433] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that flexural phonons in one-dimensional systems mediate tunable long-range spin-spin interactions, with application to color centers in hexagonal boron nitride ribbons.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin-spin interactions mediated by phonons is crucial for quantum information processing in solid-state platforms.
method: The authors theoretically analyze spin-phonon coupling in a one-dimensional lattice, considering both longitudinal and flexural phonon modes, and derive effective spin-spin interaction Hamiltonians.
result: Flexural phonons produce long-range interactions that can be tuned via tensile strain, while longitudinal phonons yield only nearest-neighbor coupling.
conclusion: The tunable interactions mediated by flexural phonons in hBN ribbons provide a promising platform for quantum simulation and quantum networking with color centers.

title: Extending The Dynamic Range In Quantum Frequency Estimation With Sequential Weak Measurements
authors: Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, And Tuvia Gefen
abstract:
Author(s): Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, and Tuvia Gefen

A sequential weak measurement protocol is developed for Bayesian quantum frequency estimation with coherent spin states in which weakly entangled ancilla qubits track the sensing qubits during free evolution to suppress phase slip errors and extend the dynamic range. The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound asymptotically across a large frequency bandwidth.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022046] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A sequential weak measurement protocol for quantum frequency estimation that uses weakly entangled ancilla qubits to suppress phase slip errors and extend dynamic range, achieving Heisenberg scaling and saturating the Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Quantum frequency estimation is limited by phase slip errors that reduce dynamic range; existing protocols trade off precision for range. The authors aim to overcome this limitation using sequential weak measurements.
method: The protocol employs coherent spin states as sensing qubits and weakly entangled ancilla qubits that track the sensing qubits during free evolution. Bayesian estimation is performed from the weak measurement outcomes.
result: The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and asymptotically saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound across a large frequency bandwidth, effectively extending the dynamic range without sacrificing precision.
conclusion: Sequential weak measurements provide a practical route to high-precision, wide-dynamic-range quantum frequency estimation, with potential applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Combines the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with metabolic power to derive a quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on information extraction from neural activity, constrained by metabolic energy and quantum sensing bounds.
method: Applies quantum estimation theory and thermodynamic energy constraints to model the magnetic field sensing process in MEG.
result: Derives a metabolic quantum limit that sets an upper bound on the information capacity of MEG, linking neural energy consumption to measurement precision.
conclusion: The limit provides a fundamental benchmark for MEG performance and highlights the role of thermodynamics in biological information processing.

title: Neural Quantum States For Entanglement-depth Certification From Randomized Pauli Measurements
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

Entanglement depth quantifies how many qubits share genuine multipartite entanglement, but certification typically relies on tailored witnesses or full tomography, both of which scale poorly with system size. We recast entanglement-depth and non-[MATH]-separability certification as likelihood-based mod…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023255] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Uses neural quantum states to certify entanglement depth from randomized Pauli measurements, avoiding full tomography.
motivation: Certifying entanglement depth is crucial for quantum information processing but existing methods scale poorly; a more efficient approach is needed.
method: Trains a neural network to represent the likelihood of measurement outcomes under different separability assumptions, using randomized Pauli measurements.
result: The method can certify entanglement depth and non-separability with high accuracy using far fewer measurements than full tomography.
conclusion: Neural quantum states provide a scalable and practical tool for entanglement-depth certification in many-body systems.

title: Blind Spots Of Randomized Benchmarking Under Temporal Correlations
authors: Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, And Alexei Gilchrist
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, and Alexei Gilchrist

Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely adopted protocol for estimating the average gate fidelity in quantum hardware. However, its standard formulation relies on the assumption of temporally uncorrelated noise, an assumption often violated in current devices. In this work, we derive analytic expre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023258] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
