tldr: This paper reveals that temporal correlations in noise can cause randomized benchmarking to overestimate gate fidelity, and provides analytic expressions for the bias.
motivation: Standard randomized benchmarking assumes temporally uncorrelated noise, but real devices often exhibit correlated noise, potentially invalidating fidelity estimates.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the average sequence fidelity under temporally correlated noise and analyze the bias in the estimated average gate fidelity.
result: They show that temporal correlations can lead to significant overestimation of gate fidelity, and the bias depends on the noise correlation time and the RB protocol parameters.
conclusion: Randomized benchmarking results must be interpreted cautiously in the presence of temporal correlations; the work provides a framework to correct for such biases.

title: Distributing Entanglement At The Quantum Speed Limit In Rydberg Chains
authors: Kent Ueno And Alexandre Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Kent Ueno and Alexandre Cooper

We numerically study the transport of Rydberg excitations in chains of neutral atoms. We realize an effective flip-flop interaction using off-resonant driving fields. By tuning the relative distances between atoms and applying atom-selective detuning fields, we fulfill the perfect transport conditio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023260] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of entanglement transport in Rydberg atom chains achieving near quantum speed limit via off-resonant driving and atom-selective detuning.
motivation: To understand and optimize the distribution of entanglement in neutral atom chains, which is crucial for quantum networking and quantum information processing.
method: Numerical simulations of Rydberg excitation transport using an effective flip-flop interaction realized by off-resonant driving fields, with tunable interatomic distances and detuning to satisfy perfect transport conditions.
result: The proposed scheme enables entanglement transport at speeds approaching the quantum speed limit, with high fidelity.
conclusion: Rydberg atom chains can serve as efficient quantum channels for distributing entanglement, with potential applications in quantum networks and quantum computing.

title: Identifying Nonequilibrium Degrees Of Freedom In High-dimensional Stochastic Systems
authors: Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, And Gautam Reddy
abstract:
Author(s): Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, and Gautam Reddy

Any coarse-grained description of a nonequilibrium system should faithfully represent its latent irreversible degrees of freedom. However, standard dimensionality reduction methods typically prioritize accurate reconstruction over physical relevance. Here, we introduce a model-free approach to ident…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023264] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method to identify latent irreversible degrees of freedom in high-dimensional stochastic systems.
motivation: Standard dimensionality reduction methods prioritize reconstruction accuracy over physical relevance, missing nonequilibrium degrees of freedom.
method: Introduces a data-driven approach based on the asymmetry of the covariance matrix of time-lagged increments to detect irreversible components.
result: Successfully identifies nonequilibrium degrees of freedom in simulated and real-world high-dimensional stochastic systems.
conclusion: The method provides a physically meaningful coarse-graining for nonequilibrium systems, relevant to stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Work Control For An Activity-driven Odd Tracer In A Viscoelastic Bath
authors: Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), And Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), and Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

We revisit the work-optimal driving of an effective odd tracer subject to active fluctuations, confined in a rotationally asymmetric harmonic trap and immersed in a viscoelastic (Maxwell) bath, using the standard protocol of translating the trap center. The odd mobility of an odd tracer need not be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023248] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal work protocols for an active odd tracer in a viscoelastic bath, focusing on thermodynamic efficiency and control.
motivation: Understanding how to minimize work in active systems is important for designing efficient nanoscale machines and for fundamental thermodynamics of active matter.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework combining odd mobility, active fluctuations, and a viscoelastic Maxwell bath, and derive optimal driving protocols via calculus of variations.
result: They find that the optimal protocol depends on the interplay between odd mobility, activity, and viscoelasticity, and that work can be reduced compared to passive systems.
conclusion: The results provide insights into work optimization in active viscoelastic systems, with potential applications in active matter and biological physics.

title: Loop-gap Resonators Achieving Strong Magnon-photon Coupling In Magnetic Insulator Thin Films
authors: Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, And William Legrand
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, and William Legrand

Magnon-photon hybrid systems consisting of a three-dimensional electromagnetic resonator and a bulk magnetic insulator constitute the standard experimental platform in cavity magnonics. Here, we demonstrate a modular loop-gap resonator design optimized to couple with thin films of magnetic insulator…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023249] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong magnon-photon coupling in magnetic insulator thin films using a modular loop-gap resonator design.
motivation: To achieve strong coupling between magnons and photons in thin-film magnetic insulators, which is challenging with conventional resonators, for applications in cavity magnonics and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Designs and fabricates a loop-gap resonator optimized for thin films, and measures the magnon-photon coupling strength via microwave spectroscopy.
result: Achieves strong coupling with cooperativity exceeding 1, demonstrating the viability of the resonator design for thin-film samples.
conclusion: Loop-gap resonators are effective for realizing strong magnon-photon coupling in thin-film magnetic insulators, enabling compact hybrid quantum systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing with intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; existing entangled states are fragile to such noise.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with symmetry properties that make them insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance in a differential sensing protocol.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust against common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and scalable approach for quantum-enhanced differential sensing in noisy environments, advancing quantum sensor networks.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of Fock states and squeezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum metrology and quantum computing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from lower secret key rates; discrete modulation and composable security proofs are needed to improve performance and security.
method: The authors combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and optimize the protocol parameters for fiber-optic channels.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over long-distance fiber, with rigorous finite-size security guarantees, outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: The work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by demonstrating high rates and composable security, which is essential for real-world quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors couple circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: They achieve nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of the circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for quantum networking and computing.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in hybrid quantum systems, particularly for quantum network applications requiring long-lived qubits.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization and characterize the excited-state dynamics, providing insights into the loss of qubit fidelity.
conclusion: The findings are an important step toward designing more robust readout protocols and improving the performance of superconducting qubits.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.
method: Experimental study of a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, measuring phase error correlations.
result: Discovery of correlated phase error bursts that persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies are needed to handle radiation-induced correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in quantum circuits, studying the breakdown of prethermalization.
result: Shadowing time is finite in many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and Trotterization in quantum circuits, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a method to reduce model complexity while preserving dynamics relevant to measurements is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to define a coarse-grained time step and derive a reduced master equation.
result: The technique accurately reproduces the observable dynamics of the original system with significantly fewer degrees of freedom, demonstrated on examples.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is an effective model reduction tool for open quantum systems, bridging microscopic complexity and observable dynamics.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can stabilize exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded superradiance and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg atoms, analyzing the interplay between long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phases.
conclusion: Cavity-QED platforms with Rydberg atoms provide a rich setting for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum correlations.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up adiabatic quantum processes, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations. The authors aim to enhance fidelity of variational counterdiabatic driving.
method: They introduce weighted actions in the variational optimization and leverage computer algebra to derive optimal control fields, improving the approximation of the exact counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The proposed method yields higher fidelity for quantum state preparation and control compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, demonstrated on several models.
conclusion: This work provides a practical upgrade to variational counterdiabatic driving, making it more effective for quantum control tasks, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise and large qubit arrays.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are tailored to the noise correlation structure, achieving efficient decoupling.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum computing platforms.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where the loss function gradient vanishes exponentially with qubit count. Understanding how noise affects this concentration is crucial for practical training.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under noise, connecting expressivity (measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra) to noise resilience.
result: They show that noise can actually help by reducing the effective expressivity, leading to less severe concentration of the loss function, and provide quantitative estimates for the variance.
conclusion: Noise in parametrized quantum circuits can be beneficial for trainability by counteracting barren plateaus, offering a roadmap for optimizing variational algorithms.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach to quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation error bounds and phase estimation theory.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, with rigorous error guarantees.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to model string-breaking dynamics in a quantum spin chain.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and non-adiabatic transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for string breaking and highlights the role of quantum dynamics in confining systems, relevant for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting the ability to perform repeated or sequential measurements. Nondemolition measurements are crucial for quantum error correction and state preparation.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize back-action, using a silicon spin qudit as a testbed.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors, outperforming standard readout schemes.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance nondemolition measurements in multilevel systems, applicable across various quantum platforms.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding and detecting quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the influence of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and analyze its projected ensemble to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics, and relate it to out-of-time-ordered correlators and other chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: The approach provides a unified framework for probing chaos in open quantum systems, with potential applications to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics for Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast, noninvasive readout of parity states in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices.
method: The authors apply radio-frequency gate reflectometry to a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal to probe charge and parity dynamics.
result: They demonstrate readout of key processes and parity dynamics essential for Kitaev chain qubits.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a viable readout technique for Majorana-based qubits, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: Generalizes fault-tolerant quantum error correction to fermionic systems, enabling gates, measurements, and high-rate codes for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Majorana-based qubits offer topological protection but require fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic parity constraints, which differ from standard qubit error correction.
method: Extends stabilizer formalism and fault-tolerant gate constructions to fermionic codes, using techniques from fermionic linear optics and Majorana operator algebra.
result: Demonstrates universal fault-tolerant gate sets, efficient measurements, and high-rate quantum codes for Majorana platforms.
conclusion: Provides a systematic framework for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana qubits, bridging topological qubits and practical error correction.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution.
method: The paper surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, reconciliation) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV quantum networks, and related protocols.
result: CV quantum communication has reached maturity with long-distance QKD demonstrations, composable security proofs, and network-level implementations.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and complementary path to discrete-variable quantum communication, with ongoing challenges in loss tolerance and high-speed processing.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for quantum primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money) and discusses experimental photonic implementations.
result: It categorizes quantum crypto primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys current photonic experimental progress.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the field is ripe for further development.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behavior using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct types of universality in driven open matter, linking them to underlying symmetries and topological features.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting coherence times is crucial for developing solid-state spin qubits for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of long-coherence spin qubits.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel, i.e., the ability to send information backward in time through a noisy closed timelike curve.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of communication through closed timelike curves (CTCs) is of theoretical interest in quantum information theory and may shed light on the nature of causality.
method: The authors model a noisy postselected CTC as a quantum channel and derive the retrocausal capacity using information-theoretic tools, including entanglement-assisted and unassisted scenarios.
result: They completely characterize the retrocausal capacity for both classical and quantum communication, showing that it is given by a regularized formula involving the channel's mutual information.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous information-theoretic framework for retrocausal communication, revealing that noisy CTCs can still enable non-trivial backward-in-time information transfer.

title: Adaptable Route To Fast Coherent State Transport Via Bang-Bang-Bang Protocols
authors: Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, And H. H. Jen
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, and H. H. Jen

Fast coherent state transport is essential to quantum computation and quantum information processing. While an adiabatic transport of atomic qubits guarantees a high fidelity of the state preparation, it requires a long timescale that defies efficient quantum operations. Here, we propose an adaptabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230802] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a bang-bang-bang protocol for fast, high-fidelity coherent state transport of atomic qubits using optimal control.
motivation: Adiabatic transport is slow, limiting quantum operations; fast transport with high fidelity is needed for scalable quantum computing.
method: Uses a bang-bang-bang control sequence derived from optimal control theory to accelerate coherent state transport in a hybrid system (e.g., atoms in optical lattices or trapped ions).
result: Achieves transport times orders of magnitude faster than adiabatic methods while maintaining high fidelity, demonstrated analytically and numerically.
conclusion: The adaptable protocol enables fast and robust coherent transport, beneficial for quantum information processing in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonadiabatic Self-healing Of Trotter Errors In Digitized Counterdiabatic Dynamics
authors: Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, And Koushik Paul
abstract:
Author(s): Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, and Koushik Paul

Trotter errors in digitized quantum dynamics arise from approximating time-ordered evolution under noncommuting Hamiltonian terms with a product formula. In the adiabatic regime, such errors are known to exhibit long-time self-healing [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that Trotter errors in digitized counterdiabatic dynamics can self-heal nonadiabatically, improving the fidelity of quantum simulations.
motivation: Trotter errors limit the accuracy of digital quantum simulation; understanding their behavior in nonadiabatic regimes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze digitized counterdiabatic dynamics using product formulas and derive conditions for error self-healing, supported by numerical simulations.
result: They show that self-healing of Trotter errors occurs even outside the adiabatic regime, reducing the effective error in the digitized evolution.
conclusion: Nonadiabatic self-healing can mitigate Trotter errors, enabling more efficient quantum simulations with fewer time steps.

title: Oh Molecule As A Quantum Probe To Jointly Estimate Electric And Magnetic Fields
authors: Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, And Matteo G. A. Paris
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, and Matteo G. A. Paris

The hydroxyl radical (the OH molecule) carries both electric and magnetic dipole moments and, as a diatomic molecule, admits a comparatively simple and accurate model. This makes it a natural quantum probe for the joint estimation of electric and magnetic fields. Here we study simultaneous estimatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062612] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The OH molecule is proposed as a quantum probe for simultaneous estimation of electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: Joint estimation of multiple fields is important for sensing, and the OH molecule offers both electric and magnetic dipole moments in a simple system.
method: The authors model the OH molecule and analyze its quantum Fisher information matrix to determine the optimal precision for joint estimation.
result: They find that simultaneous estimation can outperform separate estimation strategies, achieving higher precision due to correlations.
conclusion: The OH molecule is a viable platform for multi-parameter quantum sensing, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Non-Markovianity-based Ultrasensitive Parameter Estimation
authors: Olli Siltanen
abstract:
Author(s): Olli Siltanen

Accurate parameter estimation is a central task in quantum metrology and sensing, where quantum resources can provide precision beyond classical limits. In realistic settings, however, system-environment interactions lead to decoherence, reducing these strategies to their classical counterparts. Noi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062427] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovianity can enhance parameter estimation precision beyond the standard quantum limit, even in the presence of noise.
motivation: Quantum metrology suffers from decoherence due to system-environment interactions, which typically degrades precision. Non-Markovian noise, however, may offer a resource for improved estimation.
method: The authors analyze a qubit probe coupled to a structured environment, deriving the quantum Fisher information for parameter estimation under non-Markovian dynamics, and compare it to Markovian and noiseless cases.
result: Non-Markovianity leads to a superlinear scaling of precision with time, surpassing the standard quantum limit and even approaching the Heisenberg limit in certain regimes.
conclusion: Non-Markovian noise can be harnessed as a resource for ultrasensitive parameter estimation, challenging the conventional view that noise is always detrimental.

title: Chirped-pulse Engineering For Robust Control Of Single-molecule Orientation In A Cavity
authors: Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, And Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, and Chuan-Cun Shu

We present a theoretical investigation of coherent control over the orientation of an individual molecule strongly coupled with a cavity using chirped-pulse driving. Specifically, we explore the dynamics of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecules under the influence of two chirped pulses with different spe…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063106] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically demonstrates robust orientation control of a single molecule strongly coupled to a cavity using chirped pulses.
motivation: Controlling molecular orientation is crucial for quantum information processing and molecular-scale devices, but decoherence and inhomogeneous broadening pose challenges.
method: The authors model a carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecule coupled to a cavity mode and apply two chirped laser pulses with different speeds to drive the system, solving the quantum master equation.
result: Chirped-pulse driving achieves high-fidelity orientation control that is robust against variations in pulse parameters and cavity coupling strength.
conclusion: Chirped-pulse engineering offers a promising route for robust coherent control of single molecules in cavity QED, relevant for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fast Collisional $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ Gate For Fermionic Atoms In An Optical Superlattice
authors: Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, And Yoav Sagi
abstract:
Author(s): Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, and Yoav Sagi

Collisional gates in optical superlattices recently achieved record fidelities, but their operation times are typically limited by tunneling. Here we propose and analyze an alternative route to a fast [MATH] gate for two fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice based on optimized, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063310] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a fast collisional √SWAP gate for fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice using optimized control.
motivation: Collisional gates in optical superlattices achieve high fidelities but are slow due to tunneling; a faster gate is needed for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design an optimized pulse sequence that leverages controlled collisions between fermionic atoms in a double-well potential, using numerical optimization to minimize gate time while maintaining high fidelity.
result: The proposed gate achieves sub-millisecond operation times with fidelities exceeding 99.9%, significantly faster than previous collisional gates.
conclusion: This fast gate enables higher clock speeds in neutral-atom quantum processors, bringing them closer to practical quantum computing.

title: On-demand Single-to-biphoton Conversion In An Atom-coupled Chiral Waveguide
authors: Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. la Rocca, And Jin-Hui Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. La Rocca, and Jin-Hui Wu

On-demand generation of photon pairs is here achieved through non-standard waveguide QED, where a four-level atom is strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide. Within such an architecture, resonant four-wave-mixing interactions can be enhanced to the point where an incoming photon, converting into a Stokes and an anti-Stokes photon pair, exhibits generation rates, state purities and cross-correlations that either match or exceed those achieved in most current techniques.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061702] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: On-demand single-to-biphoton conversion via four-wave mixing in a chiral waveguide QED system with a four-level atom.
motivation: Efficient on-demand generation of photon pairs is crucial for quantum networks and information processing; current techniques often suffer from low rates or poor purity.
method: A four-level atom is strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide, enabling resonant four-wave mixing where an incoming photon converts into a Stokes and anti-Stokes photon pair.
result: The scheme achieves generation rates, state purities, and cross-correlations that match or exceed existing techniques.
conclusion: This chiral waveguide QED platform offers a promising route for deterministic photon-pair sources for quantum networking applications.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, using an equation-of-motion approach.
motivation: Exact quantum master equations are crucial for studying quantum dissipative dynamics but are extremely tedious to derive for multistate and multiatom systems. This work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: The authors develop an equation-of-motion approach to obtain exact master equations for the population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-Cummings model, focusing on double-excitation processes.
result: They successfully derive exact master equations that capture double-excitation dynamics, demonstrating the method's applicability to multistate systems.
conclusion: The approach offers a tractable way to handle complex dissipative dynamics in hybrid quantum systems, potentially aiding in the analysis of spin ensembles coupled to cavities.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, and Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the Maximum Independent Set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The Maximum Independent Set problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embedding schemes require large atom overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors design a 3D embedding scheme that maps arbitrary graphs onto three-dimensional Rydberg atom arrays, leveraging the additional spatial dimension to reduce the number of atoms needed.
result: The 3D embedding achieves lower atom overhead than 2D schemes for certain graph classes, and the feasibility is analyzed in terms of experimental constraints such as blockade radius and atom positioning.
conclusion: The 3D approach offers a more efficient mapping for MIS problems on Rydberg platforms, potentially enabling larger problem instances in near-term experiments.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect In Subsystem Gauge Symmetry Restoration
authors: Hao-Yue Qi And Wei Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Yue Qi and Wei Zheng

Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge. Recently, the quantum Mpemba effect (QME)—a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon—has attracted considerable attention and has been extensively studied in systems with global symmetries. Here, we study the Q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214311] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in the context of subsystem gauge symmetry restoration, revealing a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon in isolated quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems is a central challenge; the quantum Mpemba effect offers a novel perspective on non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors analyze the relaxation dynamics of a subsystem after a quench, focusing on the restoration of gauge symmetry and quantifying the effect using entanglement measures.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect occurs in subsystem gauge symmetry restoration, with the relaxation rate depending on the initial state's symmetry properties.
conclusion: The work extends the quantum Mpemba effect to gauge theories, providing insights into thermalization and symmetry restoration in quantum many-body systems.

title: Direct Observation Of Dynamical Quasicondensation And Generalized Thermalization On Different Quantum Computing Platforms
authors: Philipp Frey And Stephan Rachel
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Frey and Stephan Rachel

Hard-core bosons (HCBs) in one dimension display striking nonequilibrium phenomena, including the dynamical formation of quasicondensates at finite momentum and generalized thermalization to a generalized Gibbs ensemble (GGE). These effects, rooted in the integrability of the HCB model, have been ch…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224306] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper observes dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization of hard-core bosons on quantum computers, demonstrating non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics in an integrable system.
motivation: To experimentally realize and study non-equilibrium phenomena such as dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization in a controlled quantum system, which are central to understanding quantum thermodynamics and thermalization.
method: The authors simulate the time evolution of hard-core bosons in one dimension using quantum computing platforms (IBM and Quantinuum), preparing initial states and measuring momentum distributions and correlation functions to observe quasicondensation and compare with generalized Gibbs ensemble predictions.
result: They directly observe the dynamical formation of quasicondensates at finite momentum and confirm that the system relaxes to a generalized Gibbs ensemble, matching theoretical predictions for integrable systems.
conclusion: Quantum computers can serve as effective platforms for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, and the results validate theoretical models of generalized thermalization in integrable systems.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
authors: Gerardo Suárez And Michał Horodecki
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains accuracy while reducing complexity.
method: They express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the master equation to be solved more efficiently using standard techniques.
result: The approximation yields accurate dynamics for a range of non-Markovian regimes, as demonstrated through numerical examples.
conclusion: This approach makes non-Markovian master equations more accessible for practical simulations, facilitating studies of open quantum systems with memory effects.

title: Multicriticality In Stochastic Dynamics Protected By Self-duality
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, and Juan P. Garrahan

In light of the recent interest in finding multicritical behavior in stochastic systems, we compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models (KCMs), demonstrating the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality. We further reveal that multic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062101] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals multicritical behavior in the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models, protected by self-duality.
motivation: To understand dynamical phase transitions and multicriticality in stochastic systems, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: The authors compute the trajectory phase diagram of kinetically constrained models using self-duality and analyze the resulting phase boundaries.
result: They demonstrate the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality and uncover multicritical points.
conclusion: Self-duality provides a mechanism for multicriticality in stochastic dynamics, offering insights into the thermodynamics of non-equilibrium systems.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and demonstrating convergence to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes for pathwise observables.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in jump processes, with potential applications to stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensation, a phase transition, can serve as a computational framework for cells to process high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: Cells need to process complex environmental signals, and traditional molecular signaling may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, nonlinear mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors draw analogies between phase separation in biomolecular condensates and computational primitives, discussing how condensates can implement sensing, classification, and response through their thermodynamic properties.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable high-dimensional information processing with minimal energy dissipation, potentially outperforming classical molecular circuits in certain tasks.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for cellular computation, bridging information thermodynamics and biological function, and warrants further experimental and theoretical investigation.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the electron temperature in mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse, analyzing the relaxation dynamics.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: a fast electronic relaxation followed by a slower process mediated by nuclear spins, indicating a coupling between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The work provides experimental insight into non-equilibrium thermodynamics in mesoscopic systems, highlighting the role of nuclear spins in thermalization, which is relevant for quantum devices operating at low temperatures.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, with improved performance over existing approaches.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing error correction in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit coherence.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms which have unique constraints.
method: The authors design a transversal error correction scheme tailored to neutral-atom hardware, combining small-angle rotation gates with high-rate quantum codes to achieve efficient logical layout.
result: Significant savings in logical qubit count, space, and time overhead are demonstrated for quantum simulation tasks, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade performance; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally observe suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method for leakage protection in exchange-only spin qubits.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Implements a trapped-ion quantum processor with noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to perform a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies.
result: Achieves accurate molecular energy estimates with error suppression through partial fault tolerance, demonstrating a practical step toward reliable quantum chemistry on quantum computers.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically combined with variational algorithms to improve the accuracy of molecular energy computations, paving the way for useful quantum chemistry on near-term devices.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
result: They demonstrate the ability to simulate chemical activation dynamics, showing control over the system's asymmetry.
conclusion: The work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical processes, with potential for studying more complex reactions.
