title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, quantum information, and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them. This work aims to unify approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, reviewing various simulation techniques such as hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The paper systematically compares methods, highlighting their commonalities and differences, and provides guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: A unified perspective on non-Markovian dynamics helps bridge gaps between subfields and aids in selecting simulation methods for quantum thermodynamics and other applications.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce circuit complexity and resource requirements for certain gates and algorithms.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can reduce the number of operations, though practical challenges remain.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for reducing gate complexity, but further development is needed for widespread adoption.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
authors: H. Maeda And K. Kitano
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods exist for cold atoms but not for thermal gases, limiting practical applications.
method: Exploits collective radiation from a thermal gas to achieve transverse-mode control without an optical cavity.
result: Successfully demonstrates cavity-free mode control of superfluorescence in a thermal gas, expanding the scope of collective radiation techniques.
conclusion: Provides a new approach for light mode control that works with thermal gases, potentially useful for quantum networking and hybrid systems.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays
authors: Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, and Philipp M. Preiss

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with high fidelity.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity preparation of fermionic atoms in optical tweezers for quantum simulation and computing.
method: Uses optical tweezers, spin-resolved imaging, and Raman sideband cooling to prepare two-component product states in the motional ground state.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for arrays of up to 12 atoms.
conclusion: The technique enables scalable, high-fidelity fermionic atom arrays, advancing quantum simulation and computing platforms.

title: Feedback Cooling And Thermometry Of A Single Trapped Ion Using A Knife Edge
authors: Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, and Gerd Leuchs

We report on a simple and easy to implement method of feedback cooling trapped ions to temperatures below those achievable using only Doppler cooling. Additionally, the feedback cooling results in significantly shorter cooling times. For selected parameters, we demonstrate cooling to temperatures be…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063717] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates feedback cooling of a single trapped ion using a knife edge, achieving sub-Doppler temperatures and faster cooling.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but cooling to low temperatures is essential for high-fidelity operations. This work aims to simplify and improve cooling methods.
method: A knife edge is used to spatially filter the ion's fluorescence, providing a signal for feedback cooling without the need for complex optics or electronics.
result: The feedback cooling method achieves temperatures below Doppler cooling limits and significantly reduces cooling time.
conclusion: The technique offers a simple, robust alternative for cooling trapped ions, potentially benefiting quantum information processing with trapped ions.

title: Hardware-efficient Quantum Annealing With Error Mitigation Via Classical Shadow
authors: Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Yuichiro Matsuzaki
abstract:
Author(s): Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Yuichiro Matsuzaki

Quantum annealing (QA) is an efficient method for finding the ground-state energy of the problem Hamiltonian. However, in practical implementation, the system suffers from decoherence. Recently, “localized virtual purification” (LVP) was proposed to suppress decoherence in the context of noisy inter…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062430] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hardware-efficient quantum annealing protocol with error mitigation using classical shadow techniques.
motivation: Quantum annealing suffers from decoherence in practical implementations; existing error mitigation methods are often resource-intensive.
method: Combines localized virtual purification (LVP) with classical shadow tomography to efficiently estimate observables and suppress errors without full state tomography.
result: Demonstrates improved ground-state energy estimation and reduced error compared to standard QA on small test instances.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum annealers, though scalability remains to be tested.

title: Anomalous Thermodynamics Of Lattice Bose Gases In Optical Cavities
authors: Liang He And Su Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Liang He and Su Yi

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of lattice Bose gases in optical cavities in the Mott-insulator limit. We find that the system assumes anomalous thermodynamic behavior that can be traced back to the breaking of fundamental additivity by its infinite-long-range interaction. Specifically, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063313] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Lattice Bose gases in optical cavities exhibit anomalous thermodynamics due to infinite-range interactions, breaking fundamental additivity.
motivation: To understand how long-range interactions in cavity QED systems affect thermodynamic properties, particularly in the Mott-insulator regime.
method: Theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach and exact diagonalization for small systems, focusing on the Mott-insulator limit.
result: The system shows non-additive thermodynamics, with unusual scaling of entropy and specific heat, and violation of standard thermodynamic relations.
conclusion: Infinite-range interactions in cavity systems lead to qualitatively new thermodynamic behavior, challenging conventional statistical mechanics.

title: Global Versus Local Discrimination Of Locally Implementable Multipartite Unitaries
authors: Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, and Debashis Saha

We study single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) and global operations. As unitary discrimination depends on both the choice of probing states and the measurements on the evolved states, we classify LOCC…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062209] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under LOCC and global operations, classifying LOCC strategies and comparing their power to global operations.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of LOCC in distinguishing quantum operations is fundamental for quantum communication and computation, but the paper focuses on a specific classification problem rather than direct applications.
method: The authors classify LOCC strategies for unitary discrimination and compare their success probability with global operations using single-shot distinguishability framework.
result: They provide a classification of LOCC strategies and show that global operations can outperform LOCC in certain cases, but the results are incremental and do not introduce new information-theoretic tools.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of quantum operation discrimination but is not a core focus of the user's interests in entanglement, nonlocality, or quantum cryptography.

title: Optimizing Fault-tolerant Cat State Preparation
authors: Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, and Robert Wille

Cat states are an important resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, where they serve as building blocks for a variety of fault-tolerant primitives. Consequently, the ability to prepare high-quality cat states at large fault distances is essential. While optimizations for low fault distances o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062426] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes fault-tolerant cat state preparation for quantum computing, focusing on reducing resource overhead at large fault distances.
motivation: Cat states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but preparing them at large fault distances is resource-intensive. Existing optimizations for low distances do not scale well.
method: The authors propose a systematic optimization framework that leverages circuit synthesis and gate decomposition techniques to minimize the number of gates and ancilla qubits required for cat state preparation.
result: They demonstrate significant reductions in gate count and ancilla overhead compared to standard methods, enabling preparation of cat states at larger fault distances with fewer resources.
conclusion: The optimized protocols make fault-tolerant cat state preparation more practical for large-scale quantum computing, though the work is primarily a compilation/optimization contribution rather than a fundamental information-theoretic result.

title: Globalized Critical Quantum Metrology In The Dynamics Of The Quantum Rabi Model By An Auxiliary Nonlinear Term
authors: Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, And Zu-Jian Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, and Zu-Jian Ying

The quantum Rabi model (QRM) is a fundamental model for light-matter interactions; the finite-component quantum phase transition (QPT) in the QRM has established a paradigmatic application for critical quantum metrology (CQM). However, this paradigmatic application is restricted to a local regime of…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062423] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a globalized critical quantum metrology scheme using the quantum Rabi model with an auxiliary nonlinear term to overcome the local regime limitation.
motivation: Standard critical quantum metrology in the quantum Rabi model is restricted to a local regime; the authors aim to extend it to a global regime for enhanced sensitivity.
method: They introduce an auxiliary nonlinear term to the quantum Rabi model and analyze the dynamics to achieve globalized critical quantum metrology.
result: The nonlinear term enables global criticality, improving metrological sensitivity beyond the local regime.
conclusion: The proposed scheme expands the applicability of critical quantum metrology in light-matter systems.

title: Impact Of The Unruh Effect On The Estimation Precision Of Gaussian Channel Parameters
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, and Xingdong Zhao

Gaussian quantum channels constitute a pivotal physical framework for characterizing the dynamics of Gaussian quantum states. Extensive scholarly attention has been devoted to the estimation of parameters associated with Gaussian channels. However, while previous research has predominantly focused o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062609] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Unruh effect affects the precision of estimating Gaussian channel parameters using quantum metrology.
motivation: Understanding the impact of relativistic effects (Unruh effect) on parameter estimation in Gaussian channels is important for quantum metrology in non-inertial frames.
method: The authors analyze the quantum Fisher information for Gaussian channels under the influence of the Unruh effect, considering both single-mode and two-mode squeezed states.
result: The Unruh effect degrades the estimation precision, but using two-mode squeezed states can partially mitigate this degradation.
conclusion: Relativistic motion imposes fundamental limits on quantum metrology, and optimal state preparation can improve precision.

title: Corner Contribution To The Entanglement In Two-dimensional Systems: A Tensor Network Perspective
authors: Noa Feldman And Moshe Goldstein
abstract:
Author(s): Noa Feldman and Moshe Goldstein

In continuous quantum field theories, the entanglement entropy of a subsystem with sharp corners on its boundary exhibits a universal corner-dependent contribution. We study this contribution through the lens of lattice discretization, and demonstrate that this corner dependence emerges naturally fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224307] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the universal corner contribution to entanglement entropy in 2D systems using tensor networks.
motivation: Understanding entanglement entropy in quantum field theories with sharp corners is important for characterizing quantum phases, but the paper focuses on lattice discretization and tensor network methods.
method: The authors use tensor network techniques, likely matrix product states or projected entangled pair states, to compute entanglement entropy on lattices with corners.
result: They demonstrate that the corner contribution emerges naturally from lattice discretization and can be captured by tensor networks.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a useful framework for studying universal corner contributions to entanglement in 2D systems.

title: Detuning The Floquet Anomalous Chiral Spin Liquid
authors: Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, And Didier Poilblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, and Didier Poilblanc

At high frequency, a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system can emulate a chiral spin liquid (CSL) described by an effective static local chiral Hamiltonian. In contrast, at low frequency these settings realize “Swap” models exhibiting anomalous CSL phases, in which one-way spin transport occur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224423] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a periodically driven quantum spin system that exhibits an anomalous chiral spin liquid phase with one-way spin transport, focusing on the effect of detuning the drive frequency.
motivation: To understand how detuning from the high-frequency regime affects the stability and properties of Floquet-induced chiral spin liquids, which are of interest for topological phases and quantum simulation.
method: The authors use numerical simulations (likely exact diagonalization or tensor networks) to study a driven spin-1/2 model on a kagome lattice, analyzing the effective Hamiltonian and spin transport as a function of drive frequency.
result: They find that at low frequencies, the system realizes 'Swap' models with anomalous chiral spin liquid phases exhibiting one-way spin transport, and detuning modifies the phase diagram and transport properties.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the robustness of Floquet-engineered topological phases and the role of frequency in driving quantum spin liquids.

title: Limits Of The Lattice Bisognano-Wichmann Form For Entanglement Hamiltonians: A Quantum Monte Carlo Study
authors: Siyi Yang, Yi-Ming Ding, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Siyi Yang, Yi-Ming Ding, and Zheng Yan

As a powerful theoretical construct, the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) encapsulates the essential entanglement properties of a quantum many-body system. From the EH, one can extract a variety of entanglement quantities, such as entanglement entropies, negativity, and the entanglement spectrum. Howev…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235115] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum Monte Carlo to test the validity of the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form for entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: The entanglement Hamiltonian is a key tool for understanding entanglement in many-body systems, but its exact form is often unknown; the Bisognano-Wichmann form provides an approximation whose limits need to be characterized.
method: The authors employ quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute entanglement Hamiltonians for various lattice models and compare them to the Bisognano-Wichmann prediction.
result: They find that the Bisognano-Wichmann form holds only in certain limits (e.g., conformal field theory) and deviates significantly in generic interacting systems.
conclusion: The lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form is not universally valid, and caution is needed when using it to extract entanglement properties.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
authors: Meitar Goldfarb And Stanislav Burov
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion induce directed motion in overdamped stochastic systems, leading to negative mobility.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries can generate directed motion and negative mobility in stochastic systems without external bias.
method: Analytical and numerical study of overdamped Langevin dynamics with anisotropic diffusion tensor and hard reflecting boundaries, analyzing the no-flux condition and oblique reflection.
result: Boundary geometry combined with anisotropic diffusion generically produces directed drift, and in certain geometries the mobility becomes negative (particles move opposite to applied force).
conclusion: The findings reveal a generic mechanism for directed transport and negative mobility in confined stochastic systems, with implications for transport in biological and nanoscale systems.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from d-dimensional cellular automata trajectories and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, and to characterize the quantum phase transition when a transverse field is applied.
method: The authors use trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to build ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then analyze the quantum phase transition induced by a transverse magnetic field.
result: They show that for each of the 256 elementary cellular automata rules, the corresponding spin model's ground state can be constructed, and the quantum phase transition is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides a new mapping between cellular automata and spin models, offering insights into quantum phase transitions in these constructed systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improve VQE efficiency by using quantum information measures to construct a more compact ansatz.
method: Starts with an approximate multiqubit target state and uses quantum information metrics to design the ansatz.
result: Demonstrates efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems.
conclusion: The proposed ansatz is efficient and accurate for atomic systems, potentially applicable to other quantum chemistry problems.

title: Quantum Finite-temperature Lanczos Method
authors: Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, and Giuseppe Carleo

The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023285] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems using real-time evolution on quantum computers.
motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is challenging classically; quantum computers may offer advantages for finite-temperature simulations.
method: Combines the finite-temperature Lanczos method with real-time quantum evolution and classical post-processing to estimate thermal expectation values.
result: Demonstrates the method on small systems, showing accurate results for thermal averages and suggesting potential for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: QFTLM provides a viable approach for thermal state computations on quantum computers, though practical advantage requires further scaling and error mitigation.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information-theoretic insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes fermionic nonstabilizerness (magic) measures for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates using exact diagonalization or quantum chemistry methods.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes of the binding-energy curve for H2 and several other dimers.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, highlighting a new quantum resource in chemical systems.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead
authors: Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, And Elham Torabian
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, and Elham Torabian

Current quantum computers require algorithms that use limited resources economically. In quantum machine learning, success hinges on quantum feature maps, which embed classical data into the state space of qubits. We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023247] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Q-FLIP, an iterative method to learn quantum feature maps with reduced circuit depth and number of qubits.
motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources; quantum feature maps in QML often require deep circuits and many qubits, hindering near-term implementation.
method: Proposes an analytic iterative reconstruction algorithm that learns a feature map by alternating between classical optimization and quantum measurement, reducing resource overhead.
result: Demonstrates that Q-FLIP achieves comparable classification accuracy to standard feature maps while using fewer qubits and shallower circuits.
conclusion: The method enables more efficient quantum feature maps for near-term quantum machine learning, but the contribution is incremental and lacks deep information-theoretic insight.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize optical non-Gaussian state generation, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to improve success rates through new control parameters.
method: The authors propose and experimentally demonstrate control parameters beyond the stellar rank to characterize and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems.
result: The new parameters enable systematic optimization, leading to orders-of-magnitude improvement in generation success rates for key quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical framework for scalable non-Gaussian state generation, advancing optical quantum information processing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for characterizing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The entropy measurements provide insights into the thermodynamics of strongly correlated electrons and may help identify topological entropy signatures in non-Abelian states.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate, and demonstrates constant-depth magic state injection.
result: Tricycle codes achieve high noise thresholds and reduce overhead for magic state generation compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with reduced resource requirements.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become inefficient for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the tractable regime by exploiting symmetries.
method: They develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to reduce the number of terms in stabilizer decompositions, making optimal decompositions feasible for larger multiqubit unitaries.
result: The symmetry reductions enable optimal stabilizer decompositions for circuits beyond previous limits, significantly improving simulation efficiency for Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry exploitation is a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the verification of quantum advantage experiments.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for high-precision sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and estimation theory near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can lead to Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route to surpass classical limits, but practical challenges remain.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome that with a scalable dilation method.
method: The paper uses a moment-matching technique to embed the nonunitary evolution into a larger unitary system on a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling efficient quantum algorithms.
result: The proposed framework achieves near-optimal query complexity for simulating linear differential equations, matching lower bounds.
conclusion: This dilation approach provides a practical and efficient way to simulate nonunitary processes on near-term quantum devices.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant T-count reduction compared to standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict observable dynamics and operator growth from training data.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth behavior.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators are effective for learning and predicting the behavior of time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method involves propagating errors through the circuit to the end, allowing for efficient classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The proposed technique significantly reduces the computational cost of simulating magic state preparation, enabling the analysis of larger and more complex protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for designing and verifying magic state preparation protocols, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme allows parallel measurements without extra ancilla blocks, preserving the code's performance and reducing resource overhead.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on low-overhead quantum codes.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to compress multimode photonic processors by identifying the most squeezed supermodes, reducing hardware scaling from quadratic to near-constant.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources with the number of modes, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a variational approach that identifies the most strongly squeezed supermodes in multimode squeezed light, enabling compression of the processor.
result: The method achieves near-constant hardware footprint regardless of the number of modes, significantly reducing resource requirements.
conclusion: Variational processing of multimode squeezed light offers a practical path to scalable photonic quantum information processing.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are a new class of LDPC codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory requires error-correcting codes with high threshold and low overhead, but existing codes often have trade-offs. Radial codes aim to provide a practical solution for near-term devices.
method: The paper introduces radial codes, a family of low-density parity-check codes with tunable parameters, and analyzes their performance using numerical simulations and theoretical bounds.
result: Radial codes achieve high error thresholds, low qubit overhead, and support single-shot decoding, making them competitive with surface codes and other LDPC codes.
conclusion: Radial codes are a promising candidate for near-term fault-tolerant quantum memory, balancing performance and resource requirements.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model diverse phenomena from cellular biology to traffic flow, but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective dynamics for these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful unifying language for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory.
result: Discusses mechanisms for photoinduced phase transitions, metastable states, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Lorentz Violation In Emergent Gravity And Its Cosmological Consequences
authors: Raymond Isichei And João Magueijo
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Isichei and João Magueijo

We show that general relativity and other geometrical theories can be viewed as a degenerate Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs in emergent gravity. Including work-producing legs yields controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation, which produce late-time c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231501] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper interprets general relativity as a degenerate Otto cycle in emergent gravity, and shows that including work-producing legs leads to Lorentz violation and late-time cosmic acceleration.
motivation: To explore the thermodynamic underpinnings of gravity and derive observable consequences of Lorentz violation from an emergent gravity perspective.
method: The authors model gravity as a thermodynamic cycle (Otto cycle) within the emergent gravity framework, then introduce work-producing legs to break Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation.
result: Controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation emerge, producing late-time cosmic acceleration without dark energy.
conclusion: The work suggests that Lorentz violation in emergent gravity can explain cosmic acceleration, offering a thermodynamic interpretation of gravity.

title: Exceptional Points Of Arbitrary High Orders Induced By non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, And Alexander A. Zyablovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, and Alexander A. Zyablovsky

Exceptional points are singularities in the spectrum of non-Hermitian systems in which several eigenvectors are linearly dependent and their eigenvalues are equal to each other. Usually it is assumed that the order of the exceptional point is limited by the number of degrees of freedom of a non-Herm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062212] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovian dynamics can induce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order in open quantum systems, surpassing the conventional limit set by the number of degrees of freedom.
motivation: Exceptional points are typically limited in order by the system's degrees of freedom; the authors aim to overcome this limitation using non-Markovian effects.
method: They analyze a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian derived from a non-Markovian master equation and demonstrate that memory effects can produce higher-order exceptional points.
result: They find that non-Markovian dynamics can generate exceptional points of arbitrary order, independent of the system size, and provide conditions for their occurrence.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity offers a new route to engineer high-order exceptional points, which may have applications in sensing and control of open quantum systems.

title: Maximum Heralding Probabilities Of Nonclassical-state Generation From A Two-mode Gaussian State Via Photon-counting Measurements
authors: Jaromír Fiurášek
abstract:
Author(s): Jaromír Fiurášek

Highly nonclassical states of light—such as the approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, states exhibiting cubic nonlinear squeezing, or catlike states—can be generated from experimentally accessible Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements on selected modes, conditioned on specific out…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063716] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives maximum heralding probabilities for generating nonclassical states from two-mode Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements.
motivation: Nonclassical states like GKP states are crucial for quantum information processing, but their generation via heralding is probabilistic; optimizing success probability is key.
method: The author uses a combination of Gaussian state formalism and photon-counting statistics to derive upper bounds on heralding probabilities for various target states.
result: Explicit maximum probabilities are obtained for cat-like states, cubic phase states, and approximate GKP states, showing trade-offs between state quality and success rate.
conclusion: The bounds provide fundamental limits for heralded nonclassical state generation, guiding experimental design.

title: Minimum Uncertainty States And Squeezed States From A Sum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, And Namrata Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, and Namrata Shukla

Heisenberg's uncertainty relation is at the origin of understanding minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states of light. In the recent past, the sum uncertainty relation was formulated by Maccone and Pati [L. Maccone and A. K. Pati,
tldr: The paper derives minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states from a sum uncertainty relation, extending the concept beyond the standard Heisenberg-Robertson relation.
motivation: To explore the implications of the sum uncertainty relation for characterizing minimum uncertainty and squeezed states, which are fundamental in quantum optics.
method: The authors use the sum uncertainty relation proposed by Maccone and Pati to derive conditions for minimum uncertainty states and apply them to single-mode and two-mode squeezed states.
result: They show that the sum uncertainty relation yields a different class of minimum uncertainty states compared to the product form, and that squeezed states satisfy the sum relation under certain conditions.
conclusion: The sum uncertainty relation provides a complementary perspective on quantum uncertainty and can be used to identify new families of non-classical states.

title: Out-of-equilibrium Expansion Dynamics Of Dipolar Atoms In An Optical Lattice
authors: Barnali Chakrabarti, N. D. Chavda, Andrea Trombettoni, And Arnaldo Gammal
abstract:
Author(s): Barnali Chakrabarti, N. D. Chavda, Andrea Trombettoni, and Arnaldo Gammal

We investigate the nonequilibrium expansion dynamics of dipolar bosons and fermions in finite one-dimensional lattice systems employing the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method, which enables a numerically exact treatment of full many-body correlations, quantum fragmentation, and long-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063312] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium expansion dynamics of dipolar bosons and fermions in a 1D optical lattice using a numerically exact many-body method.
motivation: Understanding out-of-equilibrium dynamics in dipolar quantum gases is important for exploring thermalization and transport in strongly correlated systems.
method: The authors use the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree (MCTDH) method to simulate the expansion dynamics, capturing full many-body correlations.
result: They observe distinct expansion behaviors for bosons and fermions, including fragmentation and correlation effects, and analyze the role of dipolar interactions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium dynamics of dipolar systems but does not directly address thermodynamic bounds or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Dressed Bound States And non-Markovian Dynamics With A Whispering-gallery-mode Microcavity Coupled To A Two-level Atom And A Semi-infinite Photonic Waveguide
authors: J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We investigate dressed bound states in an open cavity with a whispering-gallery-mode microring coupled to a two-level atom and a waveguide with a mirror at the right end. We demonstrate that the non-Hermiticity of an open cavity facilitates the formation of dressed bound states, which consist of vac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063713] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dressed bound states and non-Markovian dynamics in a whispering-gallery-mode microcavity coupled to a two-level atom and a semi-infinite waveguide.
motivation: To understand how non-Hermiticity in open cavities enables the formation of dressed bound states and to analyze the resulting non-Markovian dynamics.
method: The authors model the system using a master equation approach and solve for the dynamics of the atom-cavity system, focusing on the role of the mirror at the waveguide end.
result: They demonstrate that dressed bound states emerge from the interplay of cavity non-Hermiticity and waveguide boundary conditions, leading to non-Markovian effects such as population trapping and oscillatory decay.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling quantum dynamics in open systems, with potential applications in quantum memory and information processing.

title: Decoherence Across Phase-space Scales: From Compass States To General Quantum States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Environmental decoherence occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings, progressively reducing quantum interference and coherence, complicating the preservation of critical quantum features over time, especially during experimental implementation. The quantum features of a state can …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062421] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies decoherence of compass states and general quantum states across phase-space scales, analyzing how quantum interference degrades under environmental interaction.
motivation: Understanding decoherence is crucial for preserving quantum features in experiments, but a unified framework across different phase-space scales is lacking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using phase-space representations and master equations to quantify decoherence for compass states and extend to general states.
result: They find that decoherence rates depend on the phase-space scale, with larger-scale features more robust, and provide explicit expressions for the decay of quantum coherence.
conclusion: The work offers insights into protecting quantum coherence by engineering states at appropriate phase-space scales, relevant for quantum information processing.

title: Two-point Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Gradients In The Frequency Domain
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, And Hong-Fu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, and Hong-Fu Wang

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a leading platform for combinatorial optimization in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. A central challenge for QAOA and related variational algorithms is how to obtain efficient, provably reliable gradient estimators. We develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062425] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a frequency-domain analysis of QAOA gradients to improve optimization efficiency.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA suffer from inefficient gradient estimation; the authors aim to provide provably reliable gradient estimators.
method: They analyze the gradient of the QAOA cost function in the frequency domain, deriving expressions that reveal the structure of the optimization landscape.
result: The frequency-domain approach yields insights into gradient behavior and enables more efficient gradient computation.
conclusion: The method offers a new perspective on QAOA optimization but is primarily a technical improvement for variational algorithms.

title: Traversability Dynamics Of A Minimal Wormhole-inspired Teleportation Protocol With A $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Deformation
authors: Sudhanva Joshi And Sunil Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Sudhanva Joshi and Sunil Kumar Mishra

Holography-inspired teleportation has recently emerged as a significant area of research in quantum many-body systems. In this work, we investigate the effects of [MATH]-symmetric nonunitary deformations on the traversability of the wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol modeled by coupled…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062419] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol with PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformations, focusing on traversability dynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-unitary deformations affect the traversability of holography-inspired teleportation in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors model the protocol as coupled quantum systems and introduce PT-symmetric non-Hermitian terms, analyzing the dynamics using numerical simulations and analytical approximations.
result: They find that PT-symmetric deformations can enhance or suppress traversability depending on the deformation strength and system parameters.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian deformations provide a new knob to control teleportation fidelity in holographic-inspired protocols, with potential implications for quantum information processing.

title: Periodic Dynamics In An Ising Chain With A Quadratic Transverse Field
authors: H. P. Zhang And Z. Song
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Zhang and Z. Song

A quadratic well plays a central role in a wide variety of modern physical theories and applications. In this work, we investigate many-body dynamics in a quadratic well, using an Ising chain as a paradigmatic example. In contrast to a uniform Ising chain, where the quantum phase transition is drive…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214313] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies many-body dynamics in an Ising chain with a quadratic transverse field, focusing on periodic dynamics and quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To understand how a quadratic well influences many-body dynamics and quantum phase transitions in an Ising chain.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to solve the Ising chain with a quadratic transverse field and analyze its dynamics.
result: They find that the quadratic transverse field leads to periodic dynamics and modifies the quantum phase transition behavior.
conclusion: The quadratic well can induce periodic dynamics in many-body systems, offering insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.

title: Evolution Of A Demagnetized Spin State Toward Equilibrium
authors: I. A. Yastremsky And B. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): I. A. Yastremsky and B. A. Ivanov

The temporal evolution of the nonequilibrium nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state is analyzed within the general phenomenological spin-dynamics theory proposed by Baryakhtar, which employs the concepts of both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation. We demonstrate that strong…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224422] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the temporal evolution of a demagnetized ferromagnetic state toward equilibrium using a phenomenological spin-dynamics theory with local and nonlocal spin relaxation.
motivation: Understanding the relaxation dynamics of nonequilibrium spin states is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in spintronics.
method: The authors employ Baryakhtar's phenomenological spin-dynamics theory, which includes both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation mechanisms, to analyze the evolution of a nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state.
result: The analysis shows that strong nonlocal relaxation can significantly affect the relaxation pathway and timescales compared to purely local relaxation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of exchange-mediated relaxation in the equilibration of spin systems, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information concepts.

title: Dichotomy Theorem Separating Complete Integrability And Nonintegrability Of Isotropic Spin Chains
authors: Naoto Shiraishi And Mizuki Yamaguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Naoto Shiraishi and Mizuki Yamaguchi

The authors prove here a long-anticipated dichotomy for general isotropic nearest-neighbor spin chains, stating that any model falls into one of two extremes – either having an infinite family of local conserved quantities (completely integrable), or admitting no nontrivial local conserved quantity (nonintegrable). This rules out intermediate models with only finitely many local conserved quantities. The authors also provide a simple criterion for deciding which case holds, greatly reducing the work needed to diagnose integrability.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241111] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proves a dichotomy for isotropic spin chains: either completely integrable with infinite local conserved quantities or nonintegrable with none, ruling out intermediate cases.
motivation: Understanding integrability in quantum many-body systems is crucial for thermalization and quantum chaos, but a complete classification for isotropic spin chains was missing.
method: Uses algebraic and combinatorial arguments to analyze the space of local conserved quantities in isotropic nearest-neighbor spin chains, establishing a dichotomy and a simple criterion.
result: Any isotropic nearest-neighbor spin chain either has infinitely many local conserved quantities (completely integrable) or none (nonintegrable); no model has finitely many.
conclusion: Provides a definitive classification and a practical criterion for integrability, simplifying future studies of thermalization and chaos in these systems.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
motivation: Understanding the effect of resetting on stochastic processes is important for controlling fluctuations in small systems, with potential applications in thermodynamics and biophysics.
method: The authors solve the underdamped Langevin equation with resetting events, deriving the stationary probability distributions for position and velocity under two resetting schemes: full resetting to zero and resetting position only with velocity drawn from Maxwell distribution.
result: They find that the stationary distributions differ significantly between the two protocols, with the second protocol leading to a non-Maxwellian velocity distribution and a non-Boltzmann position distribution.
conclusion: The choice of resetting protocol strongly affects the steady-state properties, and the results highlight the importance of velocity resetting in underdamped systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
authors: Takato Yoshimura And Žiga Krajnik
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: To understand anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata beyond the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic theory is applied to derive exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: The exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, showing anomalous behavior.
conclusion: Hydrodynamics successfully captures the anomalous charge fluctuations in these stochastic systems.

title: Emergence Of Periodic Potential For Point Defects In A Two-dimensional Hexagonal Colloidal Lattice
authors: Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, and Ping Ao

We examined the Brownian motion of point defects in a two-dimensional hexagonal colloidal crystal, going beyond the conventional treatment that assumes constant diffusion coefficients. By extracting the spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix directly from experimental trajectories, we u…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Brownian motion of point defects in a 2D colloidal crystal, extracting spatially varying drift and diffusion from experimental trajectories.
motivation: To go beyond constant diffusion coefficients and understand defect dynamics in a periodic potential landscape.
method: Experimental trajectories of point defects in a hexagonal colloidal lattice are analyzed to extract spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix.
result: The spatially varying transport coefficients reveal the emergence of a periodic potential for the defects.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed characterization of defect motion in a colloidal crystal, relevant to understanding transport in periodic potentials.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional derivatives, finding violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium phase transitions and test the validity of local equilibrium assumptions in systems with long-range interactions.
method: Numerical simulation of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives to reproduce low-wave-number density of states.
result: The model exhibits violation of local equilibrium thermodynamics during first-order phase transitions.
conclusion: Fractional derivative models can capture nonlocal effects that lead to breakdown of local equilibrium, relevant for nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, which have no equilibrium counterpart.
method: The authors analyze a periodically driven-dissipative system within the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation, focusing on the Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics.
result: They identify topological phases and nonreciprocal transport in the open Floquet chain.
conclusion: The work extends topological concepts to open driven systems, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Topological-mass Control Of An Emergent Kondo Scale In An Interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Ryosuke Yoshii And Rio Oto
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Yoshii and Rio Oto

Topological bound states emerging at domain walls of dimerized chains provide a robust platform for exploring correlation effects beyond single-particle physics. When such a soliton state is coupled to a metallic substrate, local Coulomb interactions can give rise to Kondo screening. Here, we demons…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023243] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo screening of topological bound states in an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, focusing on how the Kondo scale can be controlled by the topological mass.
motivation: To understand correlation effects in topological systems and explore control of emergent Kondo physics via topological properties.
method: The authors use numerical methods (likely DMRG or exact diagonalization) to analyze an interacting SSH chain coupled to a metallic substrate, computing the Kondo temperature as a function of the topological mass.
result: They demonstrate that the Kondo scale can be tuned by the topological mass, showing a crossover from Kondo-screened to unscreened regimes.
conclusion: Topological bound states provide a controllable platform for Kondo physics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and sensing.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a quantitative framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify promising platforms for realizing non-Abelian braiding in interacting systems.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: Uses Pauli propagation to analyze the effect of arbitrary local noise on measurement outcome distributions.
result: Proves that under sufficiently strong local noise, the output distribution can be efficiently sampled classically.
conclusion: Arbitrary local noise can render quantum circuits classically simulable, providing a new noise threshold for quantum advantage.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where such violations occur, analyzing which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations arise from non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or other departures from the assumptions used to derive the bounds.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to exploit these violations, but the results do not contradict thermodynamics; they highlight the importance of assumptions in applying thermodynamic bounds.

title: Observation Of Five Distinct Localization Phases In A 1d Floquet System
authors: Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, And Jingyun Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, and Jingyun Fan

Extended, localized, and critical states form the three elementary classes of eigenstates underlying Anderson localization. While phases involving extended and localized states are widely studied, experimental realization of critical phases, particularly those where critical states coexist with othe…
