[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230401] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of five distinct localization phases (extended, critical, localized, and two mixed phases) in a 1D Floquet system using a photonic waveguide array.
motivation: To experimentally realize and characterize the coexistence of extended, critical, and localized states in a single disordered Floquet system, which has been theoretically predicted but not observed.
method: A 1D photonic waveguide array with engineered disorder and periodic driving (Floquet) is used to simulate the system. Light propagation is measured to extract eigenstate properties and phase boundaries.
result: Five distinct phases are identified: extended, critical, localized, extended-critical coexistence, and critical-localized coexistence, with phase transitions confirmed by scaling analysis.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a rich phase diagram beyond the standard Anderson localization paradigm, highlighting the role of Floquet engineering in realizing novel localization phases.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities with improved efficiency.
motivation: Eigenvalue spectral analysis is fundamental in quantum mechanics, but worst-case complexity can be high; the paper aims to provide a practical quantum algorithm for this task.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to isolate clusters of eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities, leveraging quantum phase estimation and amplitude amplification.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for certain spectral structures, demonstrated analytically and numerically.
conclusion: Quantum filtering offers a practical approach for spectral analysis, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and quantum chemistry.

title: Optical Tautochrone And Squeezing Dynamics In Nonuniform Lattices
authors: Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, And Konstantinos G. Makris
abstract:
Author(s): Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, and Konstantinos G. Makris

We present exact analogies between the tautochrone problem of classical mechanics and the squeezed states of quantum optics to optical lattices. Both phenomena emerge in the same physical system, that of waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings. Extension to two dimensions yields Lissajous-type tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes analogies between the classical tautochrone problem and quantum squeezing in nonuniform optical lattices, demonstrating Lissajous-type trajectories.
motivation: To explore connections between classical mechanics and quantum optics in the context of waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings.
method: The authors derive exact solutions for light propagation in nonuniform lattices, showing that the dynamics mimic both the tautochrone (isochronous) behavior and squeezed states.
result: They find that nonuniform coupling can produce isochronous oscillations and squeezing dynamics, with extensions to two dimensions yielding Lissajous patterns.
conclusion: The work reveals a deep analogy between classical and quantum phenomena, potentially useful for designing optical devices with tailored dynamics.

title: Exotic Critical States As Fractional Fermi Seas In The One-Dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, And Manuele Landini
abstract:
Author(s): Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, and Manuele Landini

Critical quantum field theories occupy a central position in modern theoretical physics for their inherent universality stemming from long-range correlations. As an example, the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) describes a wealth of one-dimensional quantum systems at low temperatures. Its behavior is…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exotic critical states in a one-dimensional Bose gas, interpreting them as fractional Fermi seas, which is a topic in ultracold atomic physics and quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To understand the nature of exotic critical states in one-dimensional Bose gases beyond the standard Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid description.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with experimental observations of a one-dimensional Bose gas to identify fractional Fermi sea signatures.
result: Demonstrates that certain critical states can be understood as fractional Fermi seas, providing a new perspective on one-dimensional quantum fluids.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of quantum criticality in one-dimensional systems and offers a new classification of exotic states.

title: Momentum-Resolved Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy As A Probe Of Nonlinear Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler
abstract:
Author(s): Duilio De Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, and Eugene Demler

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution, using a theoretical framework based on nonlinear response functions.
result: The method can access higher-order correlations and nonlinear dynamics beyond linear response, demonstrated for a model system.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for exploring nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold gases.

title: Biorthogonal Scattering And Generalized Unitarity In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, And Hee Chul Park
abstract:
Author(s): Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, and Hee Chul Park

We investigate the two-port scattering process in non-Hermitian dimer models via quantum measurements using external leads. We focus on two exemplary dimer models that preserve parity-time symmetry via spatial gain-loss balance and exhibit nonreciprocity due to directional hopping. The scattering ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062213] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models with parity-time symmetry and nonreciprocity, focusing on biorthogonal scattering and generalized unitarity.
motivation: To understand scattering processes in non-Hermitian systems, which exhibit unique properties like PT symmetry and nonreciprocity, and to develop a generalized unitarity relation.
method: The authors analyze two-port scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models using external leads, employing biorthogonal quantum mechanics and deriving scattering matrices.
result: They derive generalized unitarity relations for the scattering matrix in non-Hermitian systems and demonstrate them on dimer models with gain-loss balance and directional hopping.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding scattering in non-Hermitian systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Distillation Of Topological Boundary States Via non-Hermitian Masking
authors: Juan Kang, Chaohua Wu, Keran Li, Shuo Liu, Qinglong Zhang, And Gang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Juan Kang, Chaohua Wu, Keran Li, Shuo Liu, Qinglong Zhang, and Gang Chen

Topological boundary states are a hallmark of topological phases, yet their direct detection remains challenging when they hybridize with bulk states or fail to form isolated in-gap modes. Here, we introduce a dynamical approach for directly distilling boundary-localized states in topological lattic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063514] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A dynamical method to distill topological boundary states using non-Hermitian masking in photonic lattices.
motivation: Topological boundary states are hard to detect when they hybridize with bulk states; a direct distillation method is needed.
method: Introduces a non-Hermitian masking technique that dynamically amplifies boundary-localized states while suppressing bulk contributions.
result: Demonstrates successful distillation of topological boundary states in a photonic lattice, enabling clear detection.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical tool for probing topological phases in systems where boundary states are not isolated.

title: Loss-resistant Bright-seeded Su(1,1) Quantum Interferometer Based On Joint Detection
authors: Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, and Jietai Jing

A quantum interferometer can achieve phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit by using the nonclassical properties of the quantum state. The SU(1,1) interferometer, a commonly used quantum interferometer, can be realized by replacing the linear beam splitters in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer wit…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063712] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A loss-resistant SU(1,1) quantum interferometer using bright-seeded joint detection is proposed and analyzed.
motivation: To improve phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit while mitigating the effects of internal losses in SU(1,1) interferometers.
method: The authors design a bright-seeded SU(1,1) interferometer with joint detection and theoretically analyze its phase sensitivity and loss resistance.
result: The proposed scheme achieves sub-shot-noise phase sensitivity and is more robust to internal losses compared to conventional SU(1,1) interferometers.
conclusion: The bright-seeded joint detection scheme offers a practical way to realize loss-resistant quantum-enhanced interferometry.

title: Spin Dependence Of Charge Dynamics And Group Velocity In Chiral Molecules
authors: Riley Stuermer, Collin Vanessen, Jacob Byers, Keith Ferrer, Prasad Gudem, Diego Kienle, Jonas Fransson, And Mani Vaidyanathan
abstract:
Author(s): Riley Stuermer, Collin VanEssen, Jacob Byers, Keith Ferrer, Prasad Gudem, Diego Kienle, Jonas Fransson, and Mani Vaidyanathan

Chiral molecules are known to preferentially select electrons with a particular spin state, an effect termed chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). In this work, the transient CISS dynamics in a chiral molecule are investigated through time-dependent quantum-transport simulations, an important s…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235414] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-dependent charge dynamics and group velocity in chiral molecules via time-dependent quantum transport simulations, focusing on the CISS effect.
motivation: Understanding the transient dynamics of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) is important for spintronics and molecular electronics.
method: Time-dependent quantum-transport simulations are performed to model charge dynamics in chiral molecules.
result: The simulations reveal spin-dependent charge dynamics and group velocity effects in chiral molecules.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transient CISS effect, which may inform future spintronic device design.

title: Spectral Decimation Of Quantum Many-body Hamiltonians
authors: Feng He, Arthur Hutsalyuk, Giuseppe Mussardo, And Andrea Stampiggi
abstract:
Author(s): Feng He, Arthur Hutsalyuk, Giuseppe Mussardo, and Andrea Stampiggi

We develop a systematic theory of spectral decimation for quantum many-body Hamiltonians and show that it provides a quantitative probe of emergent symmetries in statistically mixed spectra. Building on an analytical description of statistical mixtures, we derive an explicit expression for the size …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of spectral decimation for quantum many-body Hamiltonians to probe emergent symmetries in mixed spectra.
motivation: To provide a quantitative probe of emergent symmetries in statistically mixed spectra of quantum many-body systems.
method: Derives an analytical expression for spectral decimation based on statistical mixtures of spectra.
result: Obtains an explicit expression for the size of spectral decimation and demonstrates its use as a probe.
conclusion: Spectral decimation offers a new tool for analyzing emergent symmetries in many-body systems.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064123] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a paradigmatic model to analyze the effects of quenched disorder on topological transitions, likely employing analytical or numerical methods.
result: The paper addresses issues related to defect dynamics and quenched disorder at finite-temperature topological transitions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between disorder and topological order at finite temperature.

title: Emulation Of Self-consistent non-Hermitian Quantum Formalisms
authors: Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, and R. Chitra

Hermiticity has long been a cornerstone of quantum theory, ensuring the conservation of probability and real energy spectra. Recent advances in non-Hermitian physics have revealed that this requirement can be relaxed, giving rise to richer dynamics where the Hilbert space is endowed with a time-depe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023271] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a self-consistent non-Hermitian quantum formalism and demonstrates its emulation on a quantum computer.
motivation: To extend quantum theory beyond Hermitian Hamiltonians, enabling description of open systems and gain/loss phenomena while preserving probabilistic interpretation.
method: The authors propose a formalism based on a time-dependent metric operator and implement it via a dilation method on a quantum processor.
result: They successfully emulate non-Hermitian dynamics on a quantum computer, showing agreement with theoretical predictions for a two-level system.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway to simulate non-Hermitian quantum systems on existing quantum hardware, with implications for open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Mathematical Model Of The Amoeba-inspired Combinatorial Optimization Machine For Physical Implementation And Its Equivalence To Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Yusuke Miyajima And Masahito Mochizuki
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Miyajima and Masahito Mochizuki

Information-processing algorithms inspired by survival strategies of slime molds have been intensively studied to realize combinatorial optimization machines with high computational efficiency and low power consumption. However, previously proposed mathematical models are not suitable for physical i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023269] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mathematical model for an amoeba-inspired combinatorial optimization machine and shows its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
motivation: To design a physical implementation of a slime mold-inspired optimization machine with high efficiency and low power consumption.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model suitable for physical implementation and prove its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
result: The model is shown to be equivalent to a class of recurrent neural networks, enabling potential hardware realizations.
conclusion: The proposed model bridges biological optimization algorithms and neural network architectures, offering a path toward physical optimization machines.

title: Distinct Reentrant Transitions In A Quasiperiodic Raman Lattice
authors: Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, and Yunbo Zhang

Reentrant transitions are investigated in a one-dimensional Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components. A reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase is identified, extending reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems to include critical states in addition to extended and localized states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022044] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reentrant transitions in a quasiperiodic Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on critical, extended, and localized phases.
motivation: To explore reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems beyond the usual extended-localized transitions, including critical phases.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional Raman lattice model with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components, likely using numerical methods such as exact diagonalization or transfer matrix.
result: They identify a reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase, extending the known reentrant behavior to include critical states.
conclusion: The work reveals richer phase diagrams in quasiperiodic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pathway To Kondo Physics In Quantum Wires Coupled To A Repulsive Spin Impurity And Manifestations In Ytterbium Atoms
authors: Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, and Oded Zilberberg

The Kondo effect is a paradigmatic model of strongly correlated physics, where a magnetic impurity forms a many-body singlet with a fermionic environment. The properties of this singlet depend sensitively on correlations within the environment, which are particularly pronounced in one dimension, whe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023244] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Kondo physics in quantum wires coupled to a repulsive spin impurity, with manifestations in ytterbium atoms.
motivation: To understand how correlations in a one-dimensional fermionic environment affect the Kondo effect, especially with a repulsive impurity.
method: Theoretical analysis using renormalization group and numerical methods to study the Kondo model in quantum wires.
result: The repulsive impurity leads to novel Kondo physics distinct from the standard attractive case, with signatures in transport and spectral properties.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into strongly correlated physics in one dimension and suggest experimental realizations with ultracold ytterbium atoms.

title: Convolutional Transformer Wave Functions
authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, and Markus Heyl

A new study introduces the convolutional transformer wave function, an architecture that, unlike earlier transformer-based approaches, properly harnesses the attention mechanism while respecting the symmetries of quantum systems, setting new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022040] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a convolutional transformer wave function for quantum many-body systems, achieving high accuracy on frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.
motivation: To improve neural network quantum states by incorporating symmetries and attention mechanisms for better representation of complex quantum systems.
method: Combines convolutional layers with transformer attention, respecting lattice symmetries, and trains via variational Monte Carlo.
result: Sets new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets (e.g., J1-J2 model) and quantum dynamics simulations.
conclusion: The architecture effectively captures quantum correlations and offers a powerful tool for simulating strongly correlated systems.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging standard assumptions.
motivation: To understand how domain shape affects macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries, analyzing ground state properties and phase separation using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit in certain geometries.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not hold universally in quantum spin and dimer models, with implications for understanding quantum phase transitions and emergent phenomena.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The paper reviews the concept of space-time duality in lattice systems, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their analogy with quantum computation.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems, highlighting exactly solvable models and their connections to quantum circuits.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep links to quantum computation.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic applications, and understanding their quantum properties may enable new functionalities.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum tunneling.
result: It summarizes current understanding of quantum skyrmion properties and identifies open questions.
conclusion: Quantum effects in skyrmions are an emerging area with potential for future quantum technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Crystal-Field-Tuned Spin-Flip Luminescence In ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$
authors: Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, And Abhay Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, and Abhay Shukla

Layered magnetic materials provide the opportunity for fundamental investigations of magnetism in the two-dimensional limit. [MATH], a prototype member of this family, is antiferromagnetic below 155 K and exhibits sharp photoluminescence associated with a transition between a triplet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236401] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crystal-field-tuned spin-flip luminescence in the layered antiferromagnet NiPS3, focusing on its optical and magnetic properties.
motivation: Layered magnetic materials like NiPS3 are of interest for fundamental studies of 2D magnetism, and understanding their photoluminescence can reveal spin dynamics and crystal field effects.
method: The authors perform photoluminescence spectroscopy under varying crystal fields (e.g., via pressure or doping) and analyze the spin-flip transition features.
result: They observe that the spin-flip luminescence is tunable by crystal field modifications, indicating strong coupling between magnetic and optical properties.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that NiPS3 is a platform for studying magneto-optical phenomena in 2D, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee
abstract:
Author(s): A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, and F. Massee

Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations can cause electrons to move in bunches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236501] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations cause electrons to move in bunches.
motivation: To understand how vibrational excitations affect electron transport at the atomic scale.
method: Atomic-scale measurements of electron transport in the presence of vibrational excitations.
result: Observation of electron bunching mediated by atomic-scale vibrations.
conclusion: Vibrational excitations can induce correlated electron motion, relevant for nanoscale electronics.

title: Long-Range Order In A Strictly Short-Range Quasi-2D Xy Model: When Critical Fluctuations Matter
authors: Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, And Jian-Ping Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, and Jian-Ping Lv

The phase of spins in the quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) XY model has emerged as a topic of significant interest across multiple subfields of physics. Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems despite the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at low temperatures, contradicting the conventional expectation.
conclusion: Critical fluctuations can stabilize long-range order in quasi-2D systems with short-range interactions.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Shayamal Singh and Chris H. Greene

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: Understanding three-body physics in dipolar systems is important for ultracold chemistry and quantum simulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Quantum-mechanical description of three-body interactions with anisotropic, long-range potentials, using shielding to achieve universality.
result: Prediction of observable Efimov states in shielded polar molecules.
conclusion: Efimov physics can be realized in dipolar molecular systems, offering a new platform for studying universal three-body phenomena.

title: Proper Theory Of Magnon Orbital Angular Momentum At Equilibrium
authors: Junyu Tang And Ran Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang and Ran Cheng

The orbital motion of chargeless bosons, unlike that of electrons, does not generate a magnetic moment and thus cannot directly interact with magnetic fields. To formulate the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons, we first identify its proper conjugate variable by considering the Aharonov-Cashe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper formulates the orbital angular momentum of magnons at equilibrium by identifying its conjugate variable via the Aharonov-Casher effect.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital motion does not generate a magnetic moment, making it challenging to define their orbital angular momentum. The authors aim to provide a proper theoretical framework.
method: The authors consider the Aharonov-Casher effect to identify the conjugate variable for magnon OAM and develop a theoretical formulation.
result: They derive a consistent definition of magnon OAM at equilibrium and show its physical consequences.
conclusion: The work establishes a proper theory for magnon OAM, which may have implications for spintronics and magnonics.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:
Author(s): Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, and Takahiro Shimada

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236703] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties and topological transitions of skyrmion dislocations is important for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the core structure and elastic behavior of skyrmion dislocations.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and undergo topological phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the elasticity of skyrmion lattices, challenging the traditional Kittel analogy.

title: Learning The Action For Long-Time-Step Simulations Of Molecular Dynamics
authors: Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, And Michele Ceriotti
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, and Michele Ceriotti

Machine learning can reduce the number of time steps needed to accurately predict the progress of a dynamically evolving system.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to enable longer time steps in molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are limited by small time steps due to numerical stability; the authors aim to accelerate simulations by learning the effective action for larger steps.
method: They train a machine learning model to predict the action (integrand) over longer time intervals, effectively coarse-graining the dynamics.
result: The method allows accurate simulations with significantly fewer time steps, reducing computational cost.
conclusion: Machine learning can effectively extend time steps in molecular dynamics, offering a practical acceleration technique.

title: Nanoscale Coherent Phonons With Broadband Frequency Tunability
authors: Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), And Ying Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), and Ying Jiang (江颖)

Broadband-tunable coherent phonon tips probe functional materials at nanoscale to investigate a variety of optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nanoscale coherent phonon tips with broadband frequency tunability for probing material properties.
motivation: To develop a versatile tool for investigating optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties at the nanoscale using coherent phonons.
method: The authors fabricate nanoscale tips that generate coherent phonons with tunable frequencies and use them to probe functional materials.
result: They achieve broadband frequency tunability of coherent phonons at the nanoscale.
conclusion: The technique enables nanoscale characterization of material properties via coherent phonon spectroscopy.

title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing. A critical challenge in advancing spin-and-valley-tronic devices toward quantum operation lies in achieving coherent control over the spin and valley dynamics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236701] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent spin and valley dynamics in a van der Waals heterostructure using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect, focusing on subpicosecond control for spin-and-valley-tronics.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information storage and processing, which is a key challenge in spin-and-valley-tronics.
method: The authors use time-resolved Kerr rotation spectroscopy to probe spin and valley dynamics in a monolayer WSe2/CrSBr heterostructure, leveraging the anomalous magnetic proximity effect.
result: They demonstrate subpicosecond coherent control of spin and valley pseudospin, with a long-lived coherent superposition lasting over 100 ps.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway for ultrafast coherent manipulation of spin and valley degrees of freedom, relevant for future quantum technologies.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236704] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a finite-temperature chiral spin liquid phase induced by defects.
motivation: To understand how crystallographic defects affect the stability and phase diagram of the Kitaev spin liquid, which is a candidate for topological order.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including mean-field theory or exact diagonalization, to study the model with defects.
result: A finite density of Stone-Wales defects leads to a finite-temperature phase transition into a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can stabilize chiral spin liquids in Kitaev materials, suggesting new routes to realize topological phases.

title: Persistence Of The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition With Long-Range Couplings
authors: Luis Walther, Josef Willsher, And Johannes Knolle
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Walther, Josef Willsher, and Johannes Knolle

The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition is an archetypal example of a topological phase transition, which is driven by the proliferation of vortices. In this Letter, we analyze the persistence of the BKT transition in the XY model under the influence of long-range algebraically decaying…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227102] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the persistence of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the XY model with long-range interactions, a topic in condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how long-range couplings affect the BKT transition, which is a topological phase transition driven by vortex proliferation.
method: The authors analyze the XY model with algebraically decaying long-range interactions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the BKT transition persists for a range of long-range coupling exponents, with modifications to the critical behavior.
conclusion: Long-range interactions do not destroy the BKT transition but alter its properties, providing insight into topological phase transitions in non-local systems.

title: Crossed Surface Flat Bands In Three-Dimensional Superconducting Altermagnets
authors: Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, And Jorge Cayao
abstract:
Author(s): Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, and Jorge Cayao

Higher dimensional topological phases in three-dimensional superconducting altermagnets characterized by zero-energy surface crossed flat bands indicate the interplay between altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226001] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies zero-energy surface crossed flat bands in three-dimensional superconducting altermagnets, focusing on topological phases in condensed matter.
motivation: To explore the interplay between altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries leading to higher-dimensional topological phases.
method: Theoretical analysis of surface states in a three-dimensional superconducting altermagnet model.
result: Prediction of crossed flat bands at zero energy on the surface, indicating a novel topological phase.
conclusion: The work reveals new topological phenomena in altermagnet-superconductor hybrids, relevant for condensed matter physics.

title: Nonlinear Magnetoelectric Edelstein Effect
authors: Jinxiong Jia, Longjun Xiang, Zhenhua Qiao, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jinxiong Jia, Longjun Xiang, Zhenhua Qiao, and Jian Wang

The generation of spin magnetization by linear and nonlinear Edelstein effects has so far relied solely on electric fields. Here, we propose a distinct mechanism, the nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect (NMEE), in which electric and magnetic fields act cooperatively to produce spin magnetizat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect where both electric and magnetic fields generate spin magnetization, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To propose a new mechanism for generating spin magnetization beyond the conventional electric-field-driven Edelstein effect.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model system to demonstrate the cooperative effect of electric and magnetic fields on spin magnetization.
result: The nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect is predicted, showing spin magnetization induced by combined fields.
conclusion: This work introduces a distinct mechanism for spin generation, relevant to spintronics but not to the user's research interests.

title: Accelerating Evaporative Cooling Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas By Tilting The Optical Trap With A Magnetic Field Gradient
authors: Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, And Le Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, and Le Luo

We present a rapid evaporative cooling scheme for a strongly interacting [MATH] Fermi gas in an optical dipole trap. The method uses a magnetic-field-gradient-induced tilt of the trapping potential to accelerate cooling in the unitarity-limited regime. In evaporation based only on lowerin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063314] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to accelerate evaporative cooling of a strongly interacting Fermi gas by tilting the optical trap with a magnetic field gradient.
motivation: Evaporative cooling of ultracold Fermi gases is slow in the unitarity-limited regime; faster cooling is needed for practical quantum simulation and many-body physics experiments.
method: The authors apply a magnetic field gradient to tilt the optical dipole trap, which increases the evaporation rate by enhancing the escape of high-energy atoms while maintaining low loss of low-energy atoms.
result: The tilted trap scheme achieves significantly faster cooling times compared to standard evaporation, reaching lower temperatures in a shorter duration.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical improvement for producing ultracold Fermi gases, enabling more efficient preparation for quantum simulation experiments.

title: Optical Echoes Of Light Near An Analog Black Hole
authors: Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, And Li-Gang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, and Li-Gang Wang

The light deflection under a strong gravitational field, referred to as strong gravitational lensing, provides a powerful probe of spacetime geometry. Besides, laboratory analog models are employed to study the effects of curved spacetime and explore the design of optical devices. Here, applying the…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063517] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical echoes near an analog black hole, focusing on gravitational lensing effects in a laboratory setting.
motivation: To explore strong gravitational lensing using analog models and to design optical devices that mimic curved spacetime.
method: The authors apply theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze light deflection and echo phenomena in an analog black hole system.
result: They find that optical echoes can be produced and controlled, providing insights into spacetime geometry and potential applications in optical device design.
conclusion: Analog black hole systems can effectively simulate strong gravitational lensing, offering a platform for studying general relativity and developing novel optical devices.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
authors: Nicolò Piccione
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, focusing on optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to energy nonconservation and divergent heating rates in these models; smearing the mass density operator is needed to regularize the divergence, but the smearing distribution is arbitrary.
method: The author derives conditions for optimal smearing that minimize the diffusion rate, using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: An optimal smearing function is found that minimizes the heating rate, providing a testable prediction for collapse and hybrid models.
conclusion: The work constrains the smearing distribution in these gravitational models, linking to potential experimental tests.

title: Limitations Of An Approximative Phase-space Description In Strong-field Quantum Optics
authors: Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, And Christian Saugbjerg Lange
abstract:
Author(s): Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, and Christian Saugbjerg Lange

In recent years, strong-field processes such as high-order harmonic generation (HHG) and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical states of light have become an increasingly popular field of study. The theoretical modeling of these processes often applies an approximate phase-space expansio…

result: Demonstrates nonlinear topological edge states, topological gap solitons, and self-induced topological edge states.
conclusion: Nonlinearity enriches topological physics, but the work is primarily in condensed matter and nonlinear optics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Shanshan Hu, Ziyang Li, Liya Qiao, Yuzhong Zhang, Zongzhi Zhang, And Yaowen Liu

conclusion: Hematite exhibits altermagnetic magnon properties suitable for magnonic applications, and the combined ab initio and spin dynamics approach is effective for studying such materials.

result: Spin-orbit coupling suppresses oscillations in clean systems but enhances them in disordered systems.

method: The author analyzes the twist operator expectation value in gapped and gapless systems, deriving conditions for its validity as an order parameter in higher-dimensional systems.
